| `lem:hypergraph-distinct-head-count` | The bounded-degree head-count lemma: let delta >= 2 and k <= s/4 and let H be q distinct subsets of [s] of sizes 1..delta (heads); with E the delta-sets containing a head and theta = \|E\|/C(s,delta) (theta >= q/(2^delta C(s,delta)), equality without 2^delta for delta-uniform heads), the number of subsets of [s] of size at most k containing no head is at most sum_{j<delta} C(s,j) + 2.3 C(s,k) exp(k(delta-1)/s - k theta/delta). Proof by Lovasz's form of Kruskal-Katona. For the kernel method's dense step at p >= 5 (delta = p-1, s = 15(N+1), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda))) it gives a threshold Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)) of distinct heads, against Theta_p(N^(p-1)) possible; at delta = 2 it sharpens (DH-count). | Working proof (imports Lovasz's Kruskal-Katona theorem), checked by a fresh-context reviewer (one gap, the product bound when x < j, repaired) and by exact enumeration on 90 head families (s = 12..16, delta = 2..4). Only the counting step of a p >= 5 dense criterion: the old relations at degree p-1, the separated space at p >= 5 and the rest of the ternary graph criterion are not transcribed. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-hypergraph-head-count) |
| `obs:sunflower-selector-heads` | The sunflower observation: for p >= 5, the selector block with inputs 1-(y_i+y'_j+z)^(p-1) (i <= a, j <= b), z an affine form on a set Z of at least p-3 further Boolean coordinates, has a span of dimension ab with no affine element, and under every degree-compatible monomial order every leading monomial of the span contains the p-3 largest coordinates of Z; so distinct-head counting gives no useful bound for it although its span dimension reaches about s^2/4. At p = 3 its heads are spread pairs. Fixing z leaves inputs of degree at most two (one-probe case). | Working proof (explicit echelon basis), checked by a fresh-context reviewer, with an exact check over F5 and F7 under eight monomial orders per instance; F3 control. The dimension is that of the span in the Boolean ring; the certified rank modulo old relations is not computed. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-hypergraph-head-count) |
| `thm:allprime-low-or-dense-graph-rank-exclusion` | The all-prime graph criterion: for every odd prime p (delta = p-1), a polynomial inventory and sufficiently large N, on the separated sixteen-neighbor graph with s = 15(N+1) projected coordinates, a source of M complete accuracy-one blocks with old inputs of degree at most delta (all companions and coefficient fields) has no ordinary PC refutation through D >= 2p-1 when every block's nonlinear rank r_a in P_{<=delta}/I_delta(Gamma_H) modulo affine is at most R or at least Q_*^(p) = ceil(2^delta delta C(s,delta)((delta-1)/s + 5k/N + (Lambda+1)/k)), with Lambda = log(64(M+1)), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda)), T = (p-1)(H_* + delta R) + p and TD + k <= N/10^6 (so RD <= c_p N: R <= N^sigma polylog N for polylog D, R <= c_p N for bounded D). Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)); at p = 3 it is the ternary criterion up to constants. | Working proof: transcription of the ternary low-or-dense graph criterion, with dense heads taken in the projected coordinates modulo the projected ideal and counted by the bounded-degree head-count lemma, E certified through k+delta-2, beta = f^(p-2) c maps, the all-prime basis conversion and Fermat indicators of degree p-1 on the low side. A fresh-context reviewer found one gap (heads outside the projected coordinates at delta >= 3), repaired. Exact check of the telescoping and product identities modulo Booleanity over F3, F5, F7. Leaves the window R < r_a < Q_*^(p), much wider at p >= 5; not a lower bound for refutations with window blocks. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-allprime-graph-criterion) |
| `thm:allprime-clique-graph-rank-exclusion` | The all-prime clique-head theorem: under the hypotheses of thm:allprime-low-or-dense-graph-rank-exclusion, blocks satisfying (CH_delta-hyp) for some coordinate set M of size m_*^(p) = ceil((2s/k)(5k^2/N + Lambda + log(C_delta/2))) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) also join the criterion, where (CH_delta-hyp) asks that every delta-subset of M be a leading monomial of span(inputs) + projected old ideal under the degree-then-M-weight-then-lex order. Lemma CH_delta: a head family containing all delta-subsets of an m-set leaves at most 2 C_delta binom(s,k) exp(-mk/(2s)) sets of size at most k free, with C_delta = (4(delta-1))^(delta-1) e^(1/4-(delta-1)). Random dense blocks with h >= (binom(m,delta) ln p + Lambda)/ln(1/eps_p) inputs satisfy it, eps_p = 1-(1-1/p)^delta, so the threshold for them is Theta_p((N log N)^((p-1)/2)) instead of N^(p-3/2). | Working proof, transcribing the ternary clique-head refinement; checked by a fresh-context reviewer. The random-block count uses a multilinear Schwartz-Zippel bound and a plain union bound, weaker in constants than the ternary stratified count. The old relations alone cannot satisfy the hypothesis, so a block whose input span has dimension below (2s/k) log(8(M+1)) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) never does; whether large structured common-factor blocks such as the sunflower family satisfy it is not decided, since their inputs give no coefficient on the relevant delta-subsets but cancellation against the old relations is not excluded. The window stays open at every prime. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-allprime-clique-head) |
| `obs:restriction-mixture-top-size-reduction` | Top-size lemma: a normalized mixture of pulled-back restriction designs annihilating U, where all components at sizes outside a set I annihilate U and I meets the nonzero-weight sizes only at the largest one, has a normalized sub-mixture on I annihilating U. Applied, under typicality hypothesis (T), to the ternary endpoint designs and an inventory with n random tuples at every input count: every successful PC mixture contains a degree-D PC design for the old base plus the n tuples of one input count, built from components not required to handle them. | The lemma is elementary linear algebra with a complete proof; the application is conditional on (T), dense-side rank preservation at every restriction the mixture uses, which has no union bound for families chosen after the inventory. A reduction of the sheaf-entry mixture lead to a one-count design problem, not a refutation of mixtures; the one-count problem is a special case of the window problem and may be easier. | [Top-size lemma entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-restriction-mixture-top-size) |
| `conj:wide-affine-conditioning` | Wide-conditioning conjecture: for each odd p and D there are t,Q such that ordinary unary PHP plus an affine system with linear parts independent modulo rows, every nonzero combination Q-robust on at least t rows, has no degree-D PC refutation. With the transversal special case of the constant-row clamp, a transversal meeting it excludes a compiled source; but any width-t span has dimension at most (N+2-t)(N-1) < N^2, so for about that many random blocks or more no transversal meets the hypothesis. Control: C_j=1 for j<N has width N+1 but a degree-two refutation, so robustness is needed. | Conjecture, untested beyond its recorded one-form and two-form special cases at their own parameters; the r-parameter lift it needs is unproved and the projective proof does not port. The dimension bound and union bound are proved, and the control is a checked hand refutation. The ceiling limits the conjectured sufficient condition, not transversal or other constant-substitution designs. | [Family-compatibility entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-p-complex-family-transversal) |
| `ex:random-affine-conditioning-thresholds` | Exact degree-D PC closures over F_3 for ordinary weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus M uniformly random affine equations: the least refuted M is 0 to 2 above (n+1-2D)(n-1)+1 in every run (D=2, n=3..10; D=3, n=5..7), quadratic in n; the first combination supported on at most 2D rows appears 0 to 9 equations earlier, about log_3 C(n+1,2D) before the generic count. | Finite check with seeds and scripts retained; small boards and D<=3 only, far below the compiler degree 4p-1; says nothing about p>=5 or about robustness conditions. | [Random affine conditioning entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-random-affine-conditioning) |
| `conj:random-affine-conditioning-law` | Random-conditioning law: over F_p, ordinary unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus M independent uniformly random affine equations, whose solution flat has dimension a=(n+1)(n-1)-M modulo rows, has with high probability no degree-D PC refutation when a>=2D(n-1)+c and one when a<=2D(n-1)-c'; equivalently each n-1 random equations lower the refutation degree by about one half. With the transversal special case of the constant-row clamp it would reduce the one-count problem, and exclude w.h.p. inventories of at most about n^2-2Dn blocks with uniformly distributed chosen inputs. | Conjecture: the projection count is a heuristic, not a proof; fitted over F_3 at D=2,3 on n<=10 with hardness offset 0 to 2 and no measured margin; constants may depend on D and p; untested near D=4p-1. Unary analogue and refinement of the random-subspace degree conjecture for the bit encoding. | [Random affine conditioning entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-random-affine-conditioning) |
| `conj:partial-prefix-substitution-capacity` | Partial-prefix capacity conjecture: for each odd p and K there is k, independent of n and block widths, such that for M<=n^K blocks of widths k<h_b<=n^{O(1)} with independent uniform affine inputs and S_b the first k inputs, ordinary unary PHP plus the partial-prefix images g_{b,i} prod_{j in S_b} L_{b,j}^{p-1} (i not in S_b) has w.h.p. no PC refutation of degree B_k = max(D max(1,(p-1)(k-1)), (p-1)(k+1)), D=4p-1; by the constant-row clamp this would exclude such random inventories. Motivated by the capacity count M ~ d_D/(q d_{D-e}), which leaves substitution designs uncapped as the substituted degree grows, so a capacity statement for substitution designs cannot obstruct polynomial inventories. | Conjecture; the capacity count is a heuristic whose growth matches the measured affine law with a constant factor tending to D; the binary random-clause NS check supports its independence assumption at the NS level only; trivial for bounded widths; concerns random inventories, not arbitrary ones. | [Substitution capacity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-substitution-capacity) |
| `thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction` | For odd p and K, if the odd-prime wide-clause statement holds with M=n^K and k=ceil((K+1)log n/log(p/(p-1))) - ordinary weak unary PHP plus the images g_{b,i} prod_{j in S_b} L_{b,j}^{p-1} (i not in S_b) of any M families of affine forms, for a suitable choice of \|S_b\|=min(k,h_b), has no PC refutation of degree (4p-1)(p-1)k under the parameter condition M(1-1/p)^k<1 - then no Res(lin_Fp) refutation of ordinary unary PHP^{n+1}_n has at most n^K lines. Proof: weak-base compiler, then partial-prefix substitution on S_b. | Conditional result with a complete reviewed proof of the implication; the odd-prime wide-clause statement is open, an analogue (not a special case) of the recorded binary wide-clause statement; covers ordinary PHP only; the sets S_b must be chosen suitably (a shared S refutes the hole family). | [Logarithmic-prefix reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-degree-three-first-moment) |
| `obs:degree-three-first-moment-entropy` | Entropy lemma: a per-element first moment over the degree-three conflict space bar K_3 (dimension about N^5) for nontrivial relative cubic kernels on a uniform d-subspace is below one only if fewer than 3.47*2^{d(n-d)} <= 3.47*2^{N^4/4} elements can vanish nontrivially on some d-subspace, an exponentially thin subset; at degree two the count does not obstruct since dim bar K = Theta(N^3) < d(n-d). | Working proof of the lemma; applies to single-element union bounds only, not to unions over classes, kernel subspaces or restrictions; whether the imported Kazhdan-Ziegler exponents admit the needed rank was not checked. | [Entropy lemma](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-22-degree-three-first-moment) |
| `prop:hole-family-random-choice` | For the hole family (block b_t with inputs X_{jt}-1 over all pigeons) and independent uniform k-subsets S_t with the reduction's k, the images reduce modulo collisions to deleting the cells outside the random bipartite graph G_S (hole degree k), so the image system is the weak graph PHP on G_S; if G_S is a boundary expander with delta*s/(2d) above the needed degree, the imported Miksa-Nordstrom bound excludes PC refutations of degree (4p-1)(p-1)k. | Conditional: the expansion of G_S is heuristic and the imported Miksa-Nordstrom hypotheses were not rechecked; the collision reduction and closure equivalence are checked; covers one family. | [Choice-rule entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-random-choice-rule) |
| `obs:uniform-choice-padding-refutation` | The uniform random choice of prefix sets fails: padding each of n hole blocks (real input X_{1t}-1) with about n^2 never-zero forms such as 2-X_v makes every S_b consist of fillers with probability at least 1-k/n, so Q_b = 1, each real image gives X_{1t}=0, and pigeon 1's row equation refutes at degree about (p-1)(k+1). The existential wide-clause statement survives (choose the real input). | Refutation of the uniform rule (found by the fresh-context reviewer); any choice rule must see which inputs can vanish. | [Choice-rule entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-random-choice-rule) |
| `lem:density-choice-padding-immunity` | Under the product measure mu (each pigeon an independent uniform hole), the density q(S)=mu(all inputs in S nonzero) of a block's prefix set is non-increasing in S and satisfies min_{\|S\|=k} q(S) >= min_{T in R,\|T\|<=k} q(T) - k m_0 when inputs outside R have mu-vanishing mass <= m_0; mu-null padding cannot lower the density. | Working proof; covers mu-null padding only, not padding null modulo the base. | [Density choice-rule entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-choice-rule) |
| `lem:product-measure-anticoncentration` | If every nonzero F_p-combination of affine forms L_1..L_k has at least t eta-robust rows, then under the product measure \|mu(L=v)-p^{-k}\| <= (1-c_p eta/2)^t with c_p=1-cos(2 pi/p), so mu(all L_j nonzero) <= (1-1/p)^k + p^k(1-c_p eta/2)^t. | Working proof (standard character bound, row independence under mu, Fourier inversion); reviewer checked each step. | [Density choice-rule entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-choice-rule) |
| `obs:collision-padding-refutes-density-rule` | The density-minimizing choice of prefix sets fails: fillers C_s - 2 (column sums) never vanish modulo the base but have mu-vanishing mass about 0.18, so the rule prefers them to the real input X_{1t}-1, making Q = 1 and deleting pigeon 1's cells, a refutation at degree about (p-1)(k+1); every fixed measure fails similarly since none is supported on base solutions, so a choice rule must be base-invariant up to the substituted degree. | Refutation found by the fresh-context reviewer; the existential wide-clause statement is untouched. | [Density choice-rule entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-choice-rule) |
| `obs:closed-tuple-lift-fails-three-operators` | For R=k[D_1..D_r]/(D_i^p), p odd, r>=3, and a graded R-module C with (D_i)_i: C_d -> C_(d-1)^r surjective, the closed tuples (Theta_u z(u)=0) in C_d exceed the polarized lifts (m(a) D^a w) by at least dim C_(d-1)*(r N_(p-1) - 2 N_p + r) > 0; in the matching complex this holds at d=1 for any r>=3 forms independent modulo rows and constants, however wide, so the closed-tuple r-operator form of the two-parameter lemma is false. | Refutation with a working proof (projection to first moments, count); the deficit matches exact free-module computations at (p,r)=(3,3),(3,4),(5,3),(7,3). Vanishes for r=2 or p=2, consistent with the recorded lemmas. | [Symmetric-lift entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-symmetric-lift) |
| `lem:symmetric-lift-free-modules` | Symmetric lifting lemma: on a finitely generated graded free module over R=k[D_1..D_r]/(D_i^p), every tuple (z_a)_{\|a\|=p-1} with D_i z_a/m(a) depending only on a+e_i and D_i z_((p-1)e_i)=0 is (m(a) D^a w) for some w; for a general module the symmetric tuples modulo lifts are Ext^1_R(R/m^(p-1), C) in that degree. | Working proof via a module map from J=m^(p-1) and self-injectivity of the group algebra; exact free-module checks at five (p,r) at every degree. Dade's lemma (imported, not used in the proof) turns pencil exactness at every degree into freeness; the matching complex is exact only in a degree window, so no application to it yet. | [Symmetric-lift entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-symmetric-lift) |
| `lem:symmetric-lift-cocycle-reduction` | For a graded module over R=k[D_1..D_r]/(D_i^p): symmetric tuples in C_d lift if first-order cocycles ((c_i) with D_j c_i=D_i c_j, D_i^(p-1) c_i=0) are gradients at levels d+1..d+p-1; cocycles are gradients at level s if each D_j is exact (ker D_j^(p-1) = im D_j) on the joint kernel of D_l, l>j, between levels s-1 and s. | Working proof (level-by-level construction, then elimination of one form at a time); p-1 levels whatever r is, though the width the forced-forms hypothesis needs may grow with r. The forced-forms exactness hypothesis holds on free modules and is unproved in the matching complex. | [Cocycle-reduction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-cocycle-reduction) |
| `ex:matching-symmetric-lift-width` | Exact F_3 computation in the matching complex at lemma degree d=1: symmetric tuples all lift for dense random forms at R=N=6 and R=N=9; for r disjoint forms of t rows on 7 labels t=3 fails and t=4 lifts for r=2,3,4,5 (one seed per cell), and narrow boards fail. | Finite check at one degree, one label count and one seed per cell; no growth with r seen for r<=5, not a theorem. | [Cocycle-reduction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-cocycle-reduction) |
| `ex:forced-forms-exactness-matching` | Exact F_3 computation in the matching complex (p=3, N=7 labels, levels 2 and 3): with r=2,3 disjoint forms of t rows, forced-forms exactness and cocycle lifting hold at t=5 for every number of forced forms and fail at t=4 even with no forced form (level 3, K_2 position ker D^2 = im D); dense forms on 12 and 15 rows satisfy both. | Finite check, one seed per case, d=1 and at most two forced forms; the threshold equals the amplitude theorem's one-form row condition 2(d+p-2)+1=5; below it forcing enlarges the deficit (1 to 4 at t=4). | [Forced-forms check](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-forced-forms-check) |
| `lem:single-constraint-conditioning-equivalence` | Single-constraint dichotomy: for any Boolean base B (PHP axioms unused) and fixed forms L, one constraint forbidding F != F_p^k on affine forms L, hardness of B+{L=v} at degree E for one allowed v gives hardness of B+constraint at degree E; a refutation of B+{L=v} at degree E' gives B \|- chi_v(L)=0 at degree E'+(p-1)k, so the constraint forbidding all other patterns (density 1-p^-k) is refuted. Density plays no role for one constraint; refinement of the recorded retained affine-conditioning corollary. | Working proof by substitution and multiplication by the pattern indicator; ties the one-constraint core statement to the wide-conditioning conjecture up to (p-1)k degrees; same Fermat-selector mechanism as cor:retained-affine-conditioning-gap. | [Density-principle entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-principle) |
| `obs:boolean-image-density-control` | Boolean-image control: the weak unary PHP base plus one constraint forbidding {0,1}^k for the occupancy forms C_1..C_k (density (2/p)^k<1; forms active on every row but not robust) is refuted at degree (p-1)k, using C_s^2-C_s from Booleanity and collisions. | Checked hand refutation; density below one does not replace robustness. | [Density-principle entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-principle) |
| `obs:deciding-designs-capped` | Deciding designs are capped: affine conditioning on forms spanning all linear parts mod rows fixes every cell and is refuted at degree <=2 (so affine deciding stays below the width-t dimension bound, under N^2), and multiplier conditioning on the product of satisfaction indicators costs degree sum (p-1)k_b below the base degree (about N/(2(p-1)k) constraints). Density enters only through an F_p union bound over joint patterns in the affine route; the recorded random-conditioning thresholds stay hard at total density far above one and fit the semi-regular count of Conjecture SR with Koszul terms (64.2 vs 64, 14.4 vs 14, 8.1 vs 7). Non-affine substitutions and mixtures are not covered. | Working observations assembled from recorded results (dimension bound, old-multiplier mechanism, random-conditioning thresholds) plus the point-conditioning refutation; the count is Conjecture SR's heuristic, presentation-dependent and needing robustness. | [Density-principle entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-density-principle) |
| `ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds` | Exact F_3 PC closures at D=3: weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus M random selector constraints 1-L^2 (L uniform affine; squares of linear forms, not generic quadrics) is first refuted at M=76 (n=6, three seeds) and M=185 (n=7, two seeds), exactly ceil(gamma_3/(gamma_1-1)) from the base's graded quotient dimensions with the Frobenius syzygy L(1-L^2)=0; at n=6 (seed 9060) the degree split is exactly top 4291+34M and degree<=2 part 280+M through M=75, so no degree fall precedes the crossing; refutation at the crossing is observed. | Finite check at two small sizes and one degree; strongest evidence so far for Conjecture SR relative to PHP with nonlinear generators; not a proof, and D=3 is far below the degrees the reduction needs. | [Selector semi-regularity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-selector-semiregularity) |
| `lem:selector-kernel-first-moment` | Selector kernel criterion and first-moment identity: with A=F_3[x]/(x^2, collisions, row forms), if the base has no fall through degree 3, the squares l_b^2 are independent in A_2 and ker(Phi: A_1^M -> A_3, (a_b) -> sum a_b l_b^2) equals the Frobenius kernel {(lambda_b l_b)}, then random selectors 1-L_b^2 cause no degree-3 fall; and E\|ker Phi\| = 3^(M gamma_1 - gamma_3) sum over chi in A_3^* of pi(chi)^M with pi(chi)=Pr[chi(A_1 l^2)=0]. | Working proof of the criterion and identity, and of the obstruction: column forms have l^2=0 in A, so E[#killers] >= B(1+n3^n(1-o(1)))^M and the unconditioned moment is useless; the proof must condition on the spread event dim Ann(l_b^2)=1 and union over non-Frobenius kernel tuples by span dimension. | [Selector first-moment entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-selector-first-moment) |
| `lem:selector-spread-lemma` | Spread lemma: in A=F_3[x]/(x^2, collisions, row forms) with n>=8 holes, if a linear form l has at least four pigeons with 6-robust row functions, then Ann_{A_1}(l^2) = <l>; for uniform l this fails with probability at most C(n+1,3)(C(n,6)3^{7-n})^{n-2} = 3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}. | Working proof through third differences on the triple-pigeon components of A_3, which turn e l^2 = 0 into a cyclic multilinear identity among row functions; sufficient, not necessary. | [Spread-lemma entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-spread-lemma) |
| `ex:selector-annihilator-probes` | Exact GF(3) computations in the degree-three top algebra of weak unary PHP at n=6 (gamma_1=35, gamma_3=2569): dim Ann(l^2)=1 for 100 uniform l and for all sampled l on 3 to 7 pigeons; forms on 1 or 2 pigeons and column forms have larger annihilators; sums of two uniform squares have zero annihilator in 100 samples. | Finite sampled check at one size, below the spread lemma's range n>=8. | [Spread-lemma entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-spread-lemma) |

Conditional result: with the base z-injective below D and every P_C nonempty, the hypothesis implies no PC refutation of degree D. | `lem:pencil-reduction` | Pencil reduction: over F_3, in F_3[y1,y2] with L1=y1, L2=y2, L3 = L1+L2+c3, L4 = L1-L2+c4 with (c3,c4) != (0,0) and selectors C_v = 1-L_v^2, lambda = sum C_v = 1-c3^2-c4^2+(c3+c4)y1+(c3-c4)y2 is nonconstant, the common zero set of the selectors has two points on lambda=0 separated by any tau in {y1,y2} not parallel to lambda, and {C_1..C_4} and {lambda, chi_t(tau)} derive each other at PC degree 3 (C_w = h_w lambda - kappa_w chi_t(tau) exactly), so, after substituting any affine forms, they have the same closure at every degree D >= 3 over any base. | Working proof (polynomial identities in F_3[y1,y2]); closures checked equal at n=6, D=3 in 24 cases; lowers bounded-span equivalence from degree 6 to 3 for pencils. | [Local-falls entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-local-falls) |

| `lem:closure-additivity` | Closure additivity: in the free polynomial ring with base Gamma, for F = F1 u F2, if for every d <= D the union has PC_d(F) = NS_d(F) and every NS functional of Gamma+F through d extends through D, then PC_d(F) = PC_d(F1) + PC_d(F2) and PC_D(F) cap P_<=d = PC_d(F1) + PC_d(F2) = (PC_D(F1) cap P_<=d) + (PC_D(F2) cap P_<=d): a stable union has additive closures (subspace sums, not dimension additivity over the base). | Working proof (NS spans of unions add; extension implies stability by duality). | [Additivity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-additivity) |

Each form's gamma_1 - 1 conditions split as (gamma'_1 - 1) + (N - 1). Over F_3, with no form row-constant on the smaller board: if T has maximal rank and Z_res is nondefective, Z has expected dimension when T is onto, and otherwise exactly when the coupling has maximal rank. | `lem:pattern-row-reduction` | Pattern row reduction: on the pattern algebra P(R,L) (lex-degenerate functional top algebra, faces of size <= 3 avoiding 0-above-1 and the four triple patterns), characteristic 3, R >= 4, L >= 5, the last-row split P_t = P(R-1,L)_t (+) P^last_t is exact and rank mu = rank mu' + dim(im rho + beta(ker mu')) (coupling-dual formula); the residual splits into label slices y_{R-1,c} V_c with no quotient, dim V_c = C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-1) (c=0, c>=4), C(R-1,2)(L-2)(L-3) (c=1, the minimum), C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-2) (c=2), C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-3) (c=3); by polarization rho is injective for generic forms iff M <= d_1, and ceil(capacity) <= d_1; so maximal rank is equivalent to rank mu' + dim(coupling quotient) = min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) - ML, checked at M = floor/ceil capacity; the trace capacity is below the total by more than 5, so the coupling is needed; parts 1-3 hold in any characteristic. Separately (three-row defect), in characteristic 3 on P(3,L), L >= 4, every form has rank(u -> l^2 u) <= gamma_1 - 2 (row rescalings with zero coefficient sum, or a zero row part), so the induction starts at R = 4. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; adapts lem:coupling-dual to the pattern algebra, where the residual is unconditional. | [Pattern row-reduction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-pattern-row-reduction) |
| `lem:tropical-leading-bound` | Tropical leading bound: for forms with coefficients c_{j,x} t^{w_j(x)} (generic c, integer weights) on the pattern algebra (any monomial algebra of faces), the double-point rank of generic forms over F_3bar is at least the rank of the leading matrix A_0 (each 3-face row keeps its terms of minimal t-order w_j(F) - w_j(u)); for tie-free weights A_0 has one nonzero per row, at (winning form, its heaviest cell), and its rank is the number of distinct such pairs, which is at most M(gamma_1-2) because a form's two lightest cells are never the heaviest cell of a 3-face; so tie-free weights never certify maximal rank min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) at M <= capacity, and ties are necessary. | Working proof (row scaling and semicontinuity; the simplest case of Draisma's tropical approach to secant dimensions). | [Pattern row-reduction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-pattern-row-reduction) |

| `lem:kunneth-component-locality` | Kunneth component locality: over F_3, let G be a graded commutative algebra with l^3 = 0 on G_1, and linear forms U = U_1 + ... + U_m whose spans W_i form a direct sum W; with T_i = Sym(W_i)/(cubes), T = Sym(W)/(cubes) = tensor of T_i, A_i = F_3[x_j : j in U_i]/(x_j^3), A = tensor of A_i acting by x_j -> l_j, and any homogeneous J_i in A_i, J = sum J_i A: if G is free through degree B over T (a T-linear map T (x) C -> G bijective in degrees <= B), then Tor_1^A(A/J, G)_s = [sum_i Tor_1^{A_i}(A_i/J_i, T_i) (x) prod_{k != i} T_k/J_k T_k (x) C]_s for s <= B, so every syzygy of the chosen generators of J (the union of generating sets of the J_i) is generated by G-combinations of A-syzygies (Frobenius, Koszul for selectors) and syzygies supported on one component; forms within a component may be dependent. This proves the syzygy conclusion of conj:component-hypothesis for components with independent spans under joint freeness. | Working proof (truncation, freeness and the Kunneth formula over a field) after a fresh-context review. | [Kunneth components entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-kunneth-components) |
| `ex:member-configurations-free` | Finite check on the functional top algebra over F_3 (selector tops l^2, degrees 2 and 3): generic d-dimensional spans reach the free counts C(d+1,2) and C(d+1,2)(gamma_1-d)+C(d+2,3)-d for d <= 10 at n=6 (saturating at gamma_3 for d = 11, 12) and d <= 12 at n=7; members (all or half the directions of random subspaces, d=2..5), disjoint members and four pencils equal the joint-freeness prediction and add up, with 60 random selectors adding generically up to saturation (n=6, two seeds); overlapping members (shared dimension k) fall short of member-additivity by k(d1-k)(d2-k) in degree 3, equal to the freeness prediction over the joint span; 30 pencils, 15 three-dimensional and 6 four-dimensional members at n=6 and 45 pencils at n=7 stay additive up to saturation, including 25..41 pencils at n=7 whose spans exceed gamma_1 = 48. | Finite check (exact compiled GF(3) prefix ranks). | [Kunneth components entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-23-kunneth-components) |
| `ex:component-hypothesis-injectivity-counterexample` | Counterexample to conj:component-hypothesis as summarized (local freeness = injectivity of gr R_C -> A): on the weak unary PHP top algebra over F_3 at n = 8, the recorded 4-robust occupancy pair (hole functions (2,0,2,0,1,0,1,2), (1,0,0,2,1,1,0,2) on every row) with equation constraints l_1 = b_1, l_2 = b_2 is one component (d_C = 2, w_C = 1 = number of factors, (p-1)d_C + 2w_C = 6 <= D for D >= 6) or, if the circuit grouping takes them apart, two single-form components (4 <= D for D >= 4) with nonempty allowed sets and phi_C: F_3[y1,y2]/(y^3) -> A injective in every degree (image dimensions 2, 3, 2 in degrees 1-3 and l_1^2 l_2^2 != 0 in A_4), yet Koszul-and-Frobenius generation of the syzygies of l_1, l_2 fails in degree 3 (A/(l_1,l_2)A has 19685 against the free 19682; Tor_1^T(F_3, A)_3 has dimension 3), so the conclusion fails; the prose reading (A free over gr R_C through D) excludes the pair. | Refutation of a formulation (exact normal forms; recorded Hilbert function reproduced) after a fresh-context review. | [Injectivity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-injectivity-is-not-freeness) |
| `lem:tensor-splitting-locality` | Tensor-splitting locality: in the setting of lem:kunneth-component-locality without any independence of spans and with arbitrary graded A_i-modules M_i in place of the rings T_i (C a graded vector space with trivial action, l^3 = 0 on the forms), if a graded A-linear map (tensor_i M_i) (x) C -> G (A = tensor A_i acting factorwise) is bijective in degrees <= B, then Tor_1^A(A/J, G)_s = [sum_i Tor_1^{A_i}(A_i/J_i, M_i) (x) prod_{k != i} M_k/J_k M_k (x) C]_s for s <= B, so syzygies of the union of chosen generating sets of the J_i are generated by A-syzygies and member-local ones; freeness is the case M_i = T_i, and non-free members are allowed. | Working proof (as the Kunneth lemma, without the ring T) after a fresh-context review. | [Injectivity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-injectivity-is-not-freeness) |

The new part is the lemma that a member without its own fall has only liftable syzygies, and the exact lifting of cross-member Koszul syzygies. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; a refinement of the recorded two-condition link (the component hypothesis's direct proof), whose argument steps 3 to 5 repeat. | [Column n = 10 entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-splitting-n10) |

| `prop:column-model-gale` | Column model and Gale duality: for hole functions phi_1..phi_d on n holes and the column model R = F_3[t_1..t_n]/(t_j^2, sum t_j), with W the span of 1, phi_1..phi_d in F_3^n (dimension e) and m_j the image of the j-th unit vector in V = F_3^n/W, R/(l_phi_1..l_phi_d)R is isomorphic to Sym(V)/(m_1^2, ..., m_n^2), a polynomial ring in n - e variables modulo the squares of the Gale transform of the columns (1, phi_1(j), ..., phi_d(j)); so freeness of a column span in the model is a Hilbert-function (Froberg / Alexander-Hirschowitz type) question for squares of specific linear forms. | Working proof (quotient by a space of linear forms) after a fresh-context review; the characteristic-0 apolarity to fat points is quoted as context, its characteristic-3 form unchecked. | [Gale entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-model-gale) |

| `lem:gale-group-algebra` | Gale quotient as a group-algebra quotient: in characteristic 3, with m_1..m_n spanning V (the Gale vectors of a column span), Sym(V)/(m_j^2) = T_V/(m_j^2) where T_V = Sym(V)/(v^3) is the group algebra of (Z/3)^r, since every cube of a linear form is a combination of the m_j^3 = m_j m_j^2; so the column model of a column span is squares of specific linear forms on a free group algebra, an instance of the thread's own question. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; checked numerically against the column model in six configurations. | [Worst-direction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-worst-direction) |

A tensor-decomposition proof fails because multiplicity-1 points give non-free blocks in degree 0 and truncated freeness is not a summand property. | Finite check (exhaustive up to symmetry at the stated sizes). | [Pencil entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-pencil-exhaustive) |
| `prop:column-model-summand` | Column model as a summand: the weak unary PHP top algebra A over F_3 (x_ij^2, column collisions, row sums) decomposes as a module over its column subalgebra K = F_3[C_1..C_n]/(C_j^2) as A = R (+) A_{>=1}, graded by U-degree (B = tensor over holes of F_3 + F_3 C_j + U_j with U_j = span{x_ij : i >= 1}; r_i for i >= 1 has U-degree 1 and r_0 = sum C_j - sum_{i>=1} r_i), where R = K/(sum C_j) is the column model; hence for any column span HF(A/(l)A) = HF(R/(l)R) + HF(A_{>=1}/(l)A_{>=1}), board excess = model excess + excess of A_{>=1}, and non-freeness of the model through degree t implies non-freeness of A. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; consistent with the board-versus-model comparisons at n = 8 (54 pencil classes) and n = 9 (25 robust classes). | [Column-model summand entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-model-summand) |
| `lem:functional-relative-gluing` | Functional gluing: over every field, on the functional unary base (Booleanity, row and column exclusions, row equations) with N >= max(1, 2D-1) columns and any number of rows, z is injective on the homogenized base below D (hypothesis (a) of thm:relative-gluing), by the all-field matching filtration with the row-count remark; hence constraints satisfying (b), (c), (d) on the functional top algebra G through D give no PC refutation of degree D, over the functional base and over the weak base. | Working proof: a composition of the all-field matching filtration (row hypothesis dropped as in the Lean F_2 audit), the injectivity-stability equivalence and the relative gluing theorem. | [Base-condition entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-base-condition) |
| `prop:weak-content-splitting` | Content splitting: over every field, NS annihilators of the weak unary base through degree k are functions mu on column-injective sets with sum_{j not in cols T} mu(T+(i,j)) = (1 - c_i(T)) mu(T); the extension step from k to k+1 splits over row contents c (\|c\| = k+1) into systems sum_j nu(T+(i,j)) = (2 - c_i) mu(T); 0/1 contents are exactly the functional step (solvable for N >= max(1, 2k+1)), so z-injectivity of the weak base through D (N >= 2D-1) is equivalent to solvability of every repeated-row content system with \|c\| <= D; contents with every c_i = 2 mod p are trivial, and c = 2e_a + e_b is solvable for N >= 5 outside characteristic 2. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; general repeated contents open. | [Base-condition entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-base-condition) |
| `prop:functional-column-symmetric-relations` | Functional column relations: over every field, in the functional unary top algebra G the elementary symmetric polynomials of the column sums vanish, e_k(C_1..C_N) = sum_{\|I\|=k} prod_{i in I} r_i = 0 for k >= 1; in the column model R = F[t]/(t_j^2, sum t_j), e_k is nonzero iff some zero-marginal function on k-sets has nonzero total, e.g. over F_p for k = p and N = qp + p - 1 with p not dividing q (Lucas); so R does not embed in G for those N, while it is a direct summand of the weak algebra. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Base-condition entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-base-condition) |
| `thm:weak-single-row-contents` | One-row contents: over F_p, for k >= 1 and N >= 2k+1, every annihilator mu of the degree-k NS space of the weak unary base extends on each one-row content (k+1)e_a: W_{k,k+1} nu = (1-k) mu_k is solvable, because ker W_{k,k+1}^T = Im W_{i*,k}^T with i* the largest i <= k, i = k+1 mod p (Wilson's p-rank formula and Lucas), and the weak chain W_{j-1,j} mu_j = (2-j) mu_{j-1} gives W_{i*,k} mu_k = 0 unless k = 1 mod p, where the right side vanishes. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, importing Wilson's p-rank formula for inclusion matrices (paper not read). | [Repeated-contents entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-repeated-contents) |
| `lem:weak-row-reduction` | Row reduction for the weak base: over any field, if the weak unary base on r rows and N columns is z-injective in degree k, with k+1 <= r <= m, then so is the weak base on m rows and N columns (restrict annihilators to r rows containing the content's support and use the content splitting). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Repeated-contents entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-repeated-contents) |
| `conj:weak-base-stability` | Weak base stability: over F_p, the homogenized weak unary base (Booleanity, column exclusions, row equations) on m >= D rows is z-injective below D whenever N >= 2D-1, as the functional base is by the matching-moment theorem; the PHP board has m = N+1 >= D. | Conjecture; proved for one-row contents and (p odd) for 2e_a+e_b; verified exactly over F_3 at (D,N) = (4,7) and (5,9) for every m >= D (ex:weak-base-stability-small); N >= 2D-1 sharp at D = 4. | [Repeated-contents entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-repeated-contents) |
| `ex:weak-base-stability-small` | Exact check over F_3 (Macaulay2; Singular for 5 x 9, validated on three Macaulay2 cases): dim ker(z: B_k -> B_{k+1}) of the homogenized weak unary base is 0 for all k < D on the 4 x 7 board (D = 4) and the 5 x 9 board (D = 5), hence on every board with m >= D rows at those (D, N) by row reduction; at N = 6, D = 4 the weak base (69) and the functional base (5) both fall at degree 3; control: the weak full PHP board 6 x 5 falls by 451 at degree 3. | Finite check (exact Groebner-basis Hilbert functions truncated at D). | [Repeated-contents entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-repeated-contents) |
| `thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic` | Weak base stability, quadratic range: over any field of characteristic p, the homogenized weak unary PHP base (Booleanity, column exclusions, row equations) on m >= D rows and N >= (p-1)D^2 columns is z-injective below D; so hypothesis (a) of relative gluing holds on the weak base at logarithmic degree. Proof: falls are images of Koszul H_1 of the row sums on the column tensor power (connecting map), Frobenius cycles r_i^{p-1} a e_i lift, and by the free-seed lemma the column tensor power on D rows is free over F[R]/(R^p) plus a part in degrees >= N/(D(p-1)); then row reduction. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Weak-base stability entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-weak-base-stability) |
| `lem:free-seed-tensor` | Free seed: over a field of characteristic p let T = F[R_1..R_r]/(R_i^p) with R_i primitive (graded Hopf algebra acting diagonally on tensor products); if a graded T-module W in degrees >= 0 has W_0 = F w and Ann_T(w) = 0, then for every n >= 1 and every graded T-module M in degrees >= 0, W^{(x)n} (x) M is a graded free T-module plus a summand concentrated in degrees >= n (graded self-injectivity splits T w off W, and the tensor identity makes every term with a T factor free). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; the several-form version of the recorded single-form column-tensor exactness method. | [Weak-base stability entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-weak-base-stability) |
| `thm:column-seed-freeness` | Column seeds: over a field of characteristic p, for hole functions phi_1..phi_d on [n] with 1, phi_1..phi_d linearly independent, call a hole set B a seed when products of distinct forms L_j(y) = y_0 + sum_b phi_b(j) y_b, j in B, span every degree of F[y_0..y_d]/(y_b^p); if [n] contains t+1 disjoint seeds, the column model R = F[C]/(C_j^2, sum C_j) is free over F[l_1..l_d]/(l^p), l_b = sum_j phi_b(j) C_j, through degree t. A seed exists on p-1 holes at each point of an affine basis of F^d, so multiplicity (p-1)(t+1) on an affine basis of the values suffices. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; proves the free direction of the worst-direction conjecture in a range weaker by a constant factor for fixed d. | [Column-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-seeds) |
| `lem:board-content-reduction` | Content reduction for column forms: over any field, with row 0 eliminated (x_0j = C_j - u_j) the weak unary top algebra is B/(s, r_1..r_{m-1}) with B = tensor over holes of (F + F C_j + U_j); B is graded by the row content c of its x-part, the relations and all column-type forms are homogeneous, so A = sum_c A^(c) as modules over the forms, A^(c) depends only on the rows of supp c and lives in degrees >= \|c\|; hence A on m rows is free plus degrees >= t+1 over a column span exactly when the weak algebra on min(m, t+1) rows is (Krull-Schmidt). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Board-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-board-seeds) |
| `thm:board-seed-freeness` | Board seeds: in characteristic p, if hole functions phi_1..phi_d take the points of an affine basis P_0..P_d of F^d as values with multiplicity at least (p-1)(t+1)^2 at P_0 and (p-1)(t+1) at each P_b, then the weak unary top algebra A on any number of rows is a free F[l_1..l_d]/(l^p)-module plus a part in degrees >= t+1; on t+1 rows the row sums and column forms act diagonally on the column tensor power and blocks with (t+1)(p-1) holes at P_0 and p-1 at each P_b are free seeds. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Board-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-board-seeds) |
| `cor:seeded-selector-members` | Seeded selector members: over F_3, a member of selectors 1-(L_b-v_b)^2 on the weak unary base whose linear parts are column-type forms l_b = sum_j phi_b(j) C_j, with an affine basis of values of multiplicity at least 2(D+1)^2 at one point and 2(D+1) at the others, satisfies hypothesis (c) of relative gluing through D: by board-seed freeness its top syzygies of degree <= D are A-combinations of Frobenius l_b e_b and Koszul syzygies (Kunneth for the squares in F_3[y]/(y^3)), which lift by the Frobenius lift lemma. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; replaces the worst-direction entry's conditional chain under the multiplicity condition. | [Board-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-board-seeds) |
| `lem:span-transfer` | Span transfer: in characteristic p, for a member of constraints h_k(l_1..l_d) on the weak unary base (Booleanity among the generators), with linear forms l_b over F_p and reduced h_k over F_p, if A = (T' (x) C) + Q' by a graded T'-linear isomorphism (T' = F_p[W]/(W^p) acting by W_b -> l_b, Q' in degrees >= D+1) and the member has no fall below D in its span ring F_p[y,z]/(y^p - y z^{p-1}, h_k^h), then the member satisfies hypothesis (c) of relative gluing through D, with corrections in its own ideal: member syzygies are A-combinations of images of span-ring top syzygies, which lift there and transfer through y_b -> l_b because l^p - l z^{p-1} lies in the homogenized Booleanity ideal. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Span-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-span-transfer) |
| `thm:seeded-member-condition` | Seeded members: in characteristic p, a member of reduced F_p-polynomial constraints h_k(l) in column-type forms whose values have an affine basis with multiplicities (p-1)(D+1)^2 at one point and (p-1)(D+1) at the others ((p-1)(D+1)(D+1+d) holes), and whose allowed set in F_p^d is nonempty, satisfies hypotheses (c) and (d) of relative gluing through D after adding h(l) for h in the reduced degree-order Groebner basis of (h_k) + (y^p - y); the original system is a subset of the augmented one, and reducing a constraint of degree <= D modulo y^p - y is free at degree D. Hypothesis (b) must be checked for the augmented tops. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Span-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-span-transfer) |
| `lem:occupancy-stability` | Occupancy stability: over F_p, for every m and n >= 2D-1, the homogenized occupancy system F_p[C_1..C_n, z]/(C_j^2 - C_j z, sum_j C_j - m z) (a single weak row with right-hand side m) is z-injective below D; its top algebra is the column model F_p[C]/(C_j^2, sum C_j). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; the one-row theorem's proof with chain coefficient m-j+1. | [Occupancy-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-occupancy-transfer) |
| `lem:occupancy-transfer` | Occupancy transfer: over F_p, for a column member of constraints h_k(C) (C_j = sum_i x_ij) whose system in the occupancy ring F_p[C,z]/(C_j^2 - C_j z, sum_j C_j - m z) (m the number of rows) has no fall below D, the content-0 component of every member top syzygy of degree <= D is liftable (C_j -> sum_i x_ij carries the occupancy relations into the weak base); after augmentation by a degree-order Groebner basis of the member's occupancy ideal this holds for every column member with nonempty allowed set, with no span, seed or multiplicity condition; hypothesis (b) must then hold for the augmented tops. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Occupancy-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-occupancy-transfer) |
| `prop:content-one-restriction` | Content-one restriction: over any field, the content-e_i summand of the weak unary top algebra (row 0 eliminated) is, as a module over the column algebra, the cokernel of rho: R_[n] -> sum_j R_[n]\j, f -> (f\|_{C_j=0})_j, with R_S the column model on the holes S, shifted by one degree. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Occupancy-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-occupancy-transfer) |
| `ex:restriction-injectivity-small` | Exact check over F_3 (rho_injectivity.py): the restriction map rho: R_[n] -> sum_j R_[n]\j is injective in degree t in all 24 cases with 2t < n, 3 <= n <= 11, t <= 4, and fails in five of the nine tested cases with 2t >= n: (n,t) = (4,2), (5,3), (6,3), (6,4), (8,4). | Finite check (exact ranks over F_3). | [Occupancy-transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-occupancy-transfer) |
| `thm:restriction-injectivity` | Restriction injectivity: over any field of characteristic p or 0, for n >= 2t+1, every zero-marginal function on the t-subsets of [n] is a sum of zero-extensions of zero-marginal functions on [n]\j (j = 1..n); equivalently the restriction map rho: R_[n] -> sum_j R_[n]\j of column models is injective in degree t, so 0 -> R -> sum_j R_[n]\j -> A^(e_i) -> 0 is exact for t <= (n-1)/2, with the first two terms in degree t and A^(e_i) in degree t+1. Proof by induction on t: links of zero-marginal functions are zero-marginal, and the link map Z_t -> Z_{t-1} is surjective by the Wilson kernel identification, since t-1-i* = -1 mod p. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Restriction-injectivity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-restriction-injectivity) |
| `lem:placed-pigeon-identity` | Placed pigeon: on the weak unary base with m rows, for any row i and hole j (C_j' = sum_i' x_i'j'), x_ij (C_j - z), x_ij (sum_{j' != j} C_j' - (m-1) z) and x_ij (C_j'^2 - C_j' z) lie in the homogenized base ideal, so x_ij H(C,z) = x_ij H(C,z)\|_{C_j = z} modulo it; a lifting identity for the specialized homogenized member h^h\|_{C_j=z} in the occupancy ring of the other holes (right-hand side m-1) gives an identity for x_ij times a lift on the j-th summand. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Restriction-injectivity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-restriction-injectivity) |
| `ex:placed-pigeon-falls` | Exact check over F_3 (Singular): the column member {C_1 C_2} (C_j = sum_i x_ij), whose occupancy system has no fall, falls with the weak unary base on the 3x5 (D=3), 3x7 and 4x7 (D=4) boards (dim ker z in degree 2: 5, 4, 6), while the base alone does not; the degree-2 fall at 3x7 is the span of the placed-pigeon consequences x_i1 C_2, x_i2 C_1 modulo their sums. After adding the placed-pigeon closure (x_i1 C_2, x_i2 C_1, x_i1 x_i'2) the falls equal those of the weak base on N-1 columns in all three cases (8, 21, 69). | Refutation by finite check of occupancy no-fall implying hypothesis (c); exact Groebner Hilbert functions truncated at D. | [Placed-pigeon-falls entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-placed-pigeon-falls) |
| `conj:effective-board` | Effective board: for a column member with allowed set Z in the occupancy cube, the weak unary base plus the member's placed-pigeon closure (all x_X f with X a column-injective cell set of size <= D and f vanishing on the points of Z with the holes of X occupied) falls below D exactly as the weak base on the member's effective board (holes merged or removed as Z dictates); for hole-merging members it is stable below D when the merged board has at least (p-1)D^2 columns. | Conjecture; three exact matches for the merging member {C_1 C_2} (ex:placed-pigeon-falls). | [Placed-pigeon-falls entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-placed-pigeon-falls) |
| `ex:merge-three-effective-board` | Exact check over F_3 (Singular, D = 4): the weak unary base plus the three-hole merging member {C_aC_b : a != b in {1,2,3}} and its placed-pigeon closure falls exactly as the weak base on N-2 columns on the 4x8 board (69) and the 3x9 board (0), but not on the 3x7 board (108 against 48), where the merged board has 5 < 2D-1 columns; this refutes the exact form of conj:effective-board below the stability range. | Refutation by finite check (exact Groebner Hilbert functions truncated at D). | [Effective-board review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-effective-board-review) |
| `conj:effective-board-stability` | Effective-board stability: for a column member whose placed-pigeon closure with the weak unary base is a weak base on an effective board (for a merge of a hole set H: one fat square-zero column carrying all cells of H), the closed system is z-injective below D when the effective board has at least (p-1)D^2 ordinary columns. | Conjecture; consistent with ex:placed-pigeon-falls and ex:merge-three-effective-board in their stable cases; a proof for merging members by the fat-column extension of the weak-base stability proof is proposed. | [Effective-board review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-effective-board-review) |
| `thm:fat-board-stability` | Fat-board stability: over a field of characteristic p, a weak unary board whose columns are ordinary holes or fat columns (cell sets (i,a), a in a hole set H, with every product of two distinct cells of the column a generator), with m >= D rows and at least (p-1)D^2 ordinary columns, has its homogenized base z-injective below D; the weak-base stability proof goes through with fat columns as extra square-zero tensor factors and seeds from ordinary columns. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Fat-columns entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fat-columns) |
| `cor:merging-members` | Merging members: for disjoint hole sets H_1..H_q, the weak unary base plus the merging constraints C_a C_b (a != b in a common H_s) and their placed-pigeon closure (x_ia C_b and x_ia x_i'b, all rows i, i' including i = i') generates the same homogenized ideal as a fat board; with at least (p-1)D^2 holes outside the H_s and m >= D rows it has no fall below D and no PC refutation of degree D (socle criterion), the base plus the unclosed member has no refutation of degree D, and the closed member satisfies hypothesis (c) of relative gluing (its tops are not polynomials in column sums, which matters for (b)). The closure is PC-derivable from the member at degree 3. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; proves conj:effective-board-stability for merging members in the quadratic range. | [Fat-columns entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fat-columns) |
| `thm:onto-stability` | Onto stability: over a field of characteristic p, the weak unary base on m rows and N columns together with every column equation sum_i x_ij = 1 (the weak onto system) is refuted at degree 1 if m != N mod p, and otherwise its homogenization is z-injective below D when N >= (p-1)D^2: modulo the column sums the algebra is the weak column tensor power on m-1 rows, whose row-sum syzygies are Frobenius by content reduction and free seeds, and column-sum syzygies are placed (x_ij y e'_j) by Kunneth; all lift. The weak base conditioned on an occupancy pattern with support S, after deleting the empty columns' variables (derived at degree 2; they give degree-1 falls before deletion), is the onto system on S. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Onto-stability entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-onto-stability) |
| `thm:fiber-gluing` | Fiber gluing: over a field of characteristic p, the homogenized weak unary base on m rows plus a column member (nonconstant homogenized generators f_k in C_j = sum_i x_ij and z) is z-injective below D if (i) for every hole set S with \|S\| < D the member's occupancy system specialized at C_S = z (generators f^h\|_{C_S=z} and sum_{j not in S} C_j - (m-\|S\|)z in F[C_{S^c},z]/(C_j^2 - C_j z)) is z-injective in degrees < D-\|S\|, and (ii) Koszul 1-cycles of the row sums r_1..r_{m-1} on the top algebra modulo the occupancy tops (s = sum C_j and the f_k tops) are Frobenius plus boundaries through degree D. Proof: row-sum part by (ii); member syzygies split over placed-pigeon summands O'_{S^c} (x) U^{(x)S}, and each lifts through the specialized system J_S by (i). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Fiber-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fiber-gluing) |
| `lem:sparse-row-freeness` | Sparse row freeness: over a field of characteristic p, if a column member's generators involve only the holes of H and N - \|H\| >= (p-1)(D+1)D, condition (ii) of fiber gluing holds: by content reduction to u <= D rows plus the bulk row (C_j as row 0), the top algebra modulo the member tops is a module over T_{u+1} with free seeds in H^c, free plus degrees >= D, and modulo s it is free over T_u. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Fiber-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fiber-gluing) |
| `cor:base-by-fibers` | Base by fibers: over F_p, for every m >= 1, D >= 1 and N >= (p-1)(D+1)D, the homogenized weak unary base is z-injective below D, by fiber gluing with the empty member (condition (ii) by sparse row freeness, condition (i) by occupancy stability for single weak rows with right-hand side m-\|S\|). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; reproves the quadratic weak-base stability with a slightly larger column bound and without m >= D. | [Fiber-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fiber-gluing) |
| `ex:dense-row-freeness` | Exact check over F_3 (Singular), one board row plus the bulk row: the top algebra modulo the full top ideal of the occupancy system is free over F[rho]/(rho^3) in degrees < D (excess dim (I:rho)/(I+rho^2) = 0) for the base, onto, merge C_1C_2, a linear column constraint, a selector forbidding l = v and a two-form clause, on column forms with nonzero coefficients on every hole, at N = 12, D = 3 (two seeds) and N = 16, D = 4, which meet the one-row seed bound 4D but not the range (p-1)(D+1)D; below the range (N = 3, 4, D = 4) every member has positive excess. | Finite check; content k e_1 only. | [Fiber-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fiber-gluing) |
| `conj:row-freeness` | Row freeness: over a field of characteristic p, for every column member (with its occupancy tops) and N >= (p-1)(D+1)D, Koszul 1-cycles of the row sums on the top algebra modulo the occupancy tops are Frobenius plus boundaries through degree D (condition (ii) of fiber gluing). | Conjecture; proved for sparse members (lem:sparse-row-freeness), exact one-row checks for dense members (ex:dense-row-freeness). | [Fiber-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-fiber-gluing) |
| `ex:hereditary-falls` | Exact check over F_3 at N = 12, D = 5, all 1 <= \|S\| <= 2 with N-\|S\| >= 2e+3 (246 checks per member; the single-row saturation that reduces the count to functions on the slice is asserted at every size used): for column members augmented by their full vanishing ideal I(Z), the specialization at C_S = 1 can fall: a selector forbidding l = v has 6 falling (S, e) checks at \|S\| = 1, e = 3 (seed 1), a two-form clause 1 (S of size 1, e = 3, dimension 2; seed 2), the merge C_1C_2 48 (control), a random forbidden set of density about 1/9 none; six cases recomputed independently in Singular agree. | `lem:closure-saturation` | Closure saturation: for a nonempty set Z of occupancy patterns and the set P_Z of column-injective assignments with occupancy in Z (m >= 1 rows), the polynomials of degree <= d vanishing on P_Z are exactly the direct sum over cell sets Y in rows >= 1 of x_Y times the multilinear polynomials in the other holes' C of degree <= d-\|Y\| vanishing on Z_{S(Y)} (patterns occupying the holes of Y); so the closed member (all vanishing polynomials through degree D) is generated by placed-pigeon products and has no falls below D, with top algebra gr F^{P_Z} through degree D. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Closure-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closure-gluing) |
| `thm:closure-gluing` | Closure gluing: over a field of characteristic p, for Z nonempty in the slice sum c = m mod p, the homogenized weak unary base plus the closed member M_D(Z) is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D if the Koszul 1-cycles of the row sums r_1..r_{m-1} on G = gr F^{P_Z} (associated graded functions on the allowed assignments) of degree <= D are Frobenius plus boundaries; the condition reduces to u <= D rows plus the bulk row. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Closure-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closure-gluing) |
| `prop:single-hole-member` | Single-hole member: for m >= 2, m = 1 mod p, and Z the patterns with one occupied hole, the weak base plus the closed member M_2(Z) has a PC refutation of degree 2 (r_0 r_1 lies in the ideal), so the hypothesis of closure gluing fails for every D >= 2 and N. More generally, if every pattern of Z has weight below w <= min(m, D), r_0...r_{w-1} lies in M_D(Z) and gives a refutation of degree w; a sufficient condition must use the weights of Z. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Closure-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closure-gluing) |
| `conj:closed-row-freeness` | Closed row freeness: over a field of characteristic p, if Z contains at least half of the slice {c in {0,1}^N : sum c = m mod p} (any m >= 1) and N >= (p-1)(D+1)D, then the Koszul 1-cycles of the row sums on gr F^{P_Z} through degree D are Frobenius plus boundaries (the hypothesis of closure gluing). Stated by density because forbidden-value sets of column forms over F_p cut arbitrary sets on the slice. | Conjecture; one-row exact checks at small sizes (ex:closed-row-freeness). | [Closure-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closure-gluing) |
| `ex:closed-row-freeness` | Exact check over F_3 (Singular), one board row plus the bulk row: the associated graded functions on the allowed assignments P_Z (top ideal of the point ideal) satisfy (I:rho) = I + (rho^2) in degrees < D for the base, onto, merge, a linear constraint, a selector and a two-form clause at N = 12, D = 3 (two seeds), and for onto and linear at N = 16, D = 4 (base, merge and selector timed out at 30 minutes); every member fails at N = 4, D = 4. Below the conjecture's range, and at degrees where the closure changes no summand. | Finite check; content k e_1 only, below the conjecture's range. | [Closure-gluing entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closure-gluing) |
| `conj:closed-base-splitting` | Closed-base splitting: over F_p, let B# be the homogenized weak unary base plus the closed column member M_D(Z) (all polynomials of degree <= D vanishing on the assignments with occupancy in Z), Z covering at least half the slice; for generic forms l_1..l_k of the kind conj:column-component-splitting allows, the top algebra of B# is, through degree t, free over F[l_1..l_k]/(l^p) plus a part above degree t, so hypothesis (b) of relative gluing holds with the column component in the base and the generic members as members. | Conjecture from a route review; untested. The closed column member's tops are not polynomials in column forms, so conj:column-component-splitting does not transfer. | [Closed-base review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-closed-base-review) |
| `ex:closed-base-splitting` | Exact check over F_3 on the weak unary top algebra (n holes, n+1 rows) through degree 3: modulo the top ideal of a closed column member (selector, two-form clause, merge; two seeds; and the base), the algebra satisfies HS(A#/(l_1..l_k)) = HS(A#)/(1+q+q^2)^k for k <= 4 uniform random forms in all 14 cases at n = 8, 9, including 7 where the closure changes the algebra (by up to 5940 in degree 3); the unclosed controls split too. | `thm:global-closure-gluing` | Global closure gluing: over a field of characteristic p, for D >= 1 and any nonempty set Q of column-injective assignments with total occupancy = m mod p, the homogenized weak unary base plus all polynomials of degree <= D vanishing on Q is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D if the Koszul 1-cycles of the row sums r_1..r_{m-1} on gr F^Q through degree D are Frobenius plus boundaries; hence the weak base plus any constraints of degree <= D vanishing on Q (row equations not among them) has no degree-D refutation. The hypothesis fails when Q allows at most one pigeon in row 1 (m >= 2, p >= 3, N >= p+1). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; the closure-gluing proof with an arbitrary point set. | [Global-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-global-closure) |
| `lem:slice-strictness` | Slice strictness: for a filtered algebra F of functions on a finite set with gr F = Γ, and t in F_1 with t^p = t and top s, if ker(s: Γ_e -> Γ_{e+1}) = s^{p-1} Γ_{e-p+1} for e <= D+p-2, then F_d ∩ tF = t F_{d-1} for d <= D and gr of the functions on the level set {t = 0} is Γ/sΓ through degree D (descent f -> f - t^{p-1} g + g from f = h t^{p-2}). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Sparse-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-sparse-closure) |
| `cor:slice-saturation` | Slice saturation: over a field of characteristic p, on the cube {0,1}^N or on the weak board's column-injective assignments with any number of rows, with the degree filtration and s = sum_j C_j, if N >= (p-1)(D+p-1) then the polynomials of degree <= d vanishing on {s = m} are exactly (s - m) F_{d-1} for d <= D (seed blocks of p-1 holes make gr free over F[s]/(s^p) below D+p-1; slice strictness). | Working proof after a fresh-context review (the reviewer's suggested argument). | [Sparse-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-sparse-closure) |
| `thm:sparse-closure-stability` | Sparse closure stability: over a field of characteristic p, for Z the slice patterns whose restriction to a hole set H lies in Z_H (Z nonempty) and N - \|H\| >= (p-1)(D+1)(D+p-1), the homogenized weak unary base plus the closed member M_D(P_Z) is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D: closure gluing, content reduction to u <= D rows plus the bulk row, the product of the constrained and free holes without the slice (free over T_{u+1} by seeds in the free holes), and slice strictness. | `lem:filtered-freeness-transfer` | Filtered freeness transfer: for R the functions on F_p^e (filtered by degree, gr R = T_R) mapping by a filtered algebra map into a filtered function algebra F, if gr F = Phi (+) Q with Phi graded free over T_R and Q in degrees >= n, then for every ideal J of R and d < n, F_d cap JF = sum_alpha (J cap R_{d-a_alpha}) b_alpha and gr_d(F/JF) = (Phi (x)_{T_R} gr(R/J))_d; if Phi = T_R (x) T' (x) C with T' acting through F_p-valued degree-1 elements, gr(F/JF) is free over T' below n (lifted basis spans an R-direct summand since R is semisimple; strictness). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Seeded-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-seeded-closure) |
| `thm:seeded-closure-stability` | Seeded closure stability: over a field of characteristic p, if column forms l_1..l_d have an affine basis of values P_0..P_d with multiplicity (p-1)(D+1)^2 at P_0 and (p-1)(D+1) at each P_b, then for every W in F_p^d with Z = {c in the slice : l(c) in W} nonempty, the homogenized weak unary base plus the closed member M_D(P_Z) is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D (closure gluing, content reduction, joint board seeds for row sums and forms on u+1 <= D+1 rows, filtered freeness transfer). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Seeded-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-seeded-closure) |
| `cor:seed-transfer-ranges` | Seed-transfer ranges: with filtered freeness transfer in place of slice strictness, the conclusion of cor:slice-saturation holds for N >= (p-1)(D+1) and that of thm:sparse-closure-stability for N - \|H\| >= (p-1)(D+1)^2. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Seeded-closure entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-seeded-closure) |
| `ex:generic-form-freeness` | Exact check over F_3 (Singular, graded Nakayama): the column tensor power on 2 rows and N holes is free through degree D over its row sums and d uniform random column forms up to d = 2, 4, 8, 10 at N = 12, 16, 20, 24 for D = 3 and up to d = 4, 4, 6 at N = 16, 20, 24 for D = 4, far beyond the board-seed range; it fails from d = 4, 6, 10, 12 and d = 6, 6, 8 respectively; coordinate forms fail from degree 2 and the row sums alone are free. | Finite check, one seed per size. | [Generic-form-freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-generic-form-freeness) |
| `conj:generic-form-freeness` | Generic form freeness: for each D there is c_D > 0 such that for column forms in general position with span dimension d <= c_D N - O(1), the column tensor power on few rows is free through degree D over its row sums and the forms; the threshold shrinks with D (about N/2 at D = 3 and N/4 at D = 4 at p = 3), so freeness over the full form algebra cannot carry spans of order N at the goal's degrees. | Conjecture; exact checks at p = 3, D = 3, 4 (ex:generic-form-freeness); the rate of c_D in D is unknown. | [Generic-form-freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-generic-form-freeness) |

| `conj:block-seed-stability` | Block-seed stability: over a field of characteristic p, if the column constraints factor over disjoint hole blocks B_1..B_M (each constraint involves one block's occupancy), each block's allowed set has nonconstant occupancy count and some occupied hole, and M >= (p-1)(D+1)^2, then the weak unary base plus the closed member has no falls below D and no PC refutation of degree D: constrained blocks act as seeds, as fat columns do. | Conjecture from a route review; supported by ex:pair-matching-closed-freeness and the fat-column seed computation. | [Column-component review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-component-review) |
| `lem:good-block-seeds` | Good-block seeds: for a hole block B whose allowed set Z_B contains two patterns with weights differing mod p (good), the occupancy count s_B and the row sums r_1^B..r_u^B are linearly independent in degree 1 of gr F^{P'_B} (assignments of B to u rows and a bulk row with occupancy in Z_B), and a tensor product of (p-1)(u+1) good blocks has Ann_{T_{u+1}}(1) = 0 (multilinear components). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Block-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-block-seeds) |
| `thm:block-seed-stability` | Block-seed stability: over a field of characteristic p, for a partition of the holes into blocks B_t with allowed sets Z_t and Z = {c in the slice : c_{B_t} in Z_t for all t} nonempty, if at least (p-1)(D+1)^2 blocks are good (two allowed weights differing mod p), the homogenized weak unary base plus the closed member M_D(P_Z) is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D. Contains sparse members (free holes are good blocks) and merges of a perfect matching; proves the mod-p version of conj:block-seed-stability (partial resolution; blocks with integer counts agreeing mod p, such as {0, p}, stay open). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Block-seeds entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-block-seeds) |
