| `ex:in-range-selector-freeness` | Exact check over F_3 with a compiled kernel on the direct-sum form of the closed algebra (validated against all recorded Singular values, including excess 970 for the symmetric pin): at N = 24, D = 3, in the range of closed row freeness, the one-row test passes for the base and for families of 1 to 16 selectors on independent dense random forms (spans up to 16, beyond the generic threshold of about 10); the selectors' Hilbert-function contributions are additive through degree 3 (46 each in degree 3), so they do not interact at this degree and the test does not probe entanglement. | Finite check in range at D = 3; entangled interactions not visible at this degree. | [Direct-sum search entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-direct-sum-search) |
| `lem:degreewise-gluing` | Degreewise gluing: for U, W in the Boolean cube over any field, degree-d functions on U and W agreeing on U n W glue to a degree-d function on U u W iff I_d(U n W) = I_d(U) + I_d(W) iff dim F_d(UuW) - dim F_d(U) - dim F_d(W) + dim F_d(UnW) = 0 (always <= 0); this holds for all d <= D iff the graded Mayer-Vietoris sequence of graded function modules is exact through D. In characteristic p, gluing always succeeds after a shift delta = deg of a polynomial that is 0 on U and 1 on W minus U (k(p-1) for a k-form clause with F_p data), and for n sets in a chosen order I_d(n U_i) lies in sum_{i<n} I_{d+i delta}(U_i) + I_{d+(n-1)delta}(U_n). | Working proof after a fresh-context review (hypotheses stated, n-set bound sharpened). Elementary; it identifies the Mayer-Vietoris route's exactness hypothesis, which fails on small boards. | [Interaction-locality entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-interaction-locality) |
| `ex:interaction-locality-failure` | Exact check over F_3 on the occupancy slice, dense random forms (coefficients in {1,2}), N = 8, 10, 11, d <= 4: the degreewise gluing defect is nonzero for some selector pairs (6 of 17 checks at N = 10 seed 1, 5 of 17 at N = 11) and for a pair of two-form clauses (1 of 17), and I_d of a triple intersection exceeds the sum of the pairwise ideals in 2 of 18 triple-degree cases (by 1 at N = 8, d = 2; by 2 at N = 11, d = 4). So exact locality and pairwise determination fail unconditionally; all boards are below the closed-freeness ranges. | Finite check refuting only the unconditional forms; says nothing in range. Rank and nullspace computations agree on 12 validation cases; the shift bound holds in all. | [Interaction-locality entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-interaction-locality) |
| `conj:t-wise-locality` | t-wise locality: over F_p, for clauses b = 1..M, each with k affine F_p-forms of the column occupancies, cutting allowed sets U_b of the occupancy slice, if every subfamily of at most t clauses has linearly independent combined linear parts that are jointly free through degree D (graded slice functions free over the truncated algebra of those forms), and t >= t_0(D, k, p), then I_d(n_b U_b) = sum_b I_d(U_b) for every d <= D (the vanishing ideal of the allowed set is generated degree by degree by the single clauses' ideals). The hypothesis gives this for every subfamily of at most t clauses (reduction to form space via the filtered freeness transfer lemma and product sets); independence is necessary (two selectors on one form forbidding different values fail at degree 1). | Refuted in its form-space version by the covering obstruction (every threshold, degree 1, allowed set {0}); the slice version is refuted wherever a slice carries s_0(t_0) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees <= max(D,3). A corrected version would need density of the allowed set as well; density alone fails (dense dependent families). | [Locality route review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-locality-route-review) |
| `prop:pairing-obstruction` | Pairing obstruction: over F_3, for s >= 1 and e = ceil(s/2), the s+1 selectors on F_3^s forbidding y_i = 0 (i <= s) and y_1+...+y_s = c (c = s + w_0 mod 3, w_0 = e for even s, w_0 in {e-1, e} for odd s) have every s linear parts independent, yet I_e(n U_b) != sum_b I_e(U_b), witnessed by prod (y_{2i-1} - y_{2i}) (times y_s - 1 or 2 - y_s for odd s) against the signed level measure; the same holds on the occupancy slice when the forms are jointly free in degrees <= e+2. So the form-space version of conj:t-wise-locality needs t_0(D,1,3) >= 2D+1, and the slice version needs t_0(D,1,3) >= 2D-3 (D >= 3) whenever some slice carries 2D-4 occupancy forms jointly free in degrees <= D. | Working proof after a fresh-context review and a second pass on the rewritten slice step. Specific to p = 3 and k = 1. The canonical family has no failure below ceil(s/2) for s <= 9 (computed, not claimed). | [Pairing obstruction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-pairing-obstruction) |
| `prop:covering-obstruction` | Covering obstruction: over F_3, for every t and s >= s_0(t) = O(t log t) there are M = 3s selectors on F_3^s (hyperplanes v_b.y = c_b, c_b in {1,2}) with every t of the v_b independent and allowed set exactly {0}; for any selector family with allowed set {0}, degreewise locality fails at degree 1 (I_1 of the allowed set = linear forms, single-selector ideals have no degree-1 elements), and on the slice with defect >= s when the forms are jointly free in degrees <= 3. So the form-space version of conj:t-wise-locality fails for every t_0 and D >= 1, and the slice version for every D >= 1 wherever a slice carries s_0(t_0) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees <= max(D,3). | Working proof after a fresh-context review (slice proviso corrected to degrees <= max(D,3)). Probabilistic existence; failure is by covering, with a sparse allowed set. | [Covering obstruction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-covering-obstruction) |

Density alone does not give locality. | Finite check; small form spaces cannot combine density with independence of more than two clauses of width >= 2, so the combined hypothesis is untested. | [Covering obstruction entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-covering-obstruction) |

| `conj:planted-excess-falls` | Planted excess falls (conjecture): over F_3, on the weak unary base in its degree-2 stability range, a planted family of M generic selectors (values avoiding the forms' values at a fixed matching, so satisfiable) has dim ker(z: B_1 -> B_2) = min(gamma_1, max(0, M - tau_2)), tau_2 the dimension of the degree-2 top space the selectors fill: no falls up to the count, then one derived linear consequence per extra selector until the degree-2 closure is the ideal of the planted point; random-valued families are refuted instead. | Conjecture; exact agreement at 3 rows, 18 holes (tau_2 = 1218, gamma_1 = 51) at M = 200 to 2000, one seed. | [Planted families entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-planted-families) |

| `prop:conditioned-base` | Conditioned base: over any field, for a partial matching rho on r rows of the weak unary board, the homogenized weak base plus the closed pins (x_ij - [j = rho(i)] on pinned rows, x_i'j = 0 for free rows in pinned columns) is isomorphic as a graded F[z]-algebra to the homogenized weak base on the (m-r) x (N-r) board, so under the stability theorem's hypotheses it has no falls below D when N - r >= (p-1)D^2 and m - r >= D; open pins alone fall in degree 2 (r >= 1, m >= 2, N >= 2); and restricting a degree-D PC refutation gives one of the restricted system, so lower bounds may be proved after conditioning (rho consistent with the constraints). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Conditioned base entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-conditioned-base) |
| `prop:one-count-by-freeness` | One-count by freeness: over F_3, on the weak unary base in its stability range, if each of n blocks is a satisfiable member of reduced polynomial constraints of degree <= D in its h input forms, the nh forms are linearly independent, and the weak top algebra is free through D over the truncated algebra of their joint span, then the base plus the blocks has no PC refutation of degree D (span transfer, Groebner augmentation, relative gluing with one member). For the top-size lemma's one-count problem two gaps remain: replacing the compiler's ENS blocks by members in their input forms, and freeness over about nh generic forms, while the proved seed methods reach d <= N/((p-1)(t+1)) - t - 1. | Working proof of a conditional reduction after a fresh-context review. | [One-count link entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-one-count-link) |
| `lem:seed-cap` | Seed cap: in characteristic p, if T = F[U]/(u^p), dim U = k, acting diagonally on a tensor product of \|B\| square-zero column modules F + V_j through linear maps, has Ann_T(1) = 0, then \|B\| >= (p-1)k (the top element of T has degree (p-1)k and the module has no elements above degree \|B\|); so seed-based freeness proofs with t+1 disjoint seed blocks over t+1+d directions need N >= (p-1)(t+1)(t+1+d), and the caps of the board-seed, row-rank-seed and projection-freeness theorems are intrinsic. | Working proof (degree count). | [Many-form freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-many-form-freeness) |
| `conj:maximal-generic-freeness` | Maximal generic freeness (conjecture): over F_3 the weak unary top algebra A of the PHP board is free through t over d generic linear forms whenever the prediction HS_A/(1+q+q^2)^d is nonnegative through degree t (a Froberg-type property); at n = 8 the degree-3 bound is d = 21 of gamma_1 = 63. | Conjecture; recorded evidence at n = 8, t = 3 (15 of 16 random systems with 4 to 22 forms at the expected truncated Hilbert function, one pointwise exception). | [Many-form freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-many-form-freeness) |
| `prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums` | Generic forms as row sums: in characteristic p, for d <= m linear forms with injective column maps pi_j: W -> V_j on the weak board without row sums, the algebra is, as a graded u(W)-module (u(W) = F[W]/(w^p), diagonal primitive action), a direct sum over column sets S of (u(W)/m^2)^(tensor ([N] minus S)) tensored with trivial summands in degree \|S\|, and (u(W)/m^2)^(tensor k) is the d-row weak algebra without row sums on k holes over its row sums; so freeness over such forms through t holds iff the column tensor powers (u/m^2)^(tensor (N-s)) are free through t-s. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Column tensor power entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-tensor-power) |
| `conj:column-tensor-power-freeness` | Column tensor power freeness (conjecture): over F_3 the weak algebra without row sums on d >= 1 rows and N holes is free through t over its row sums (minimal free cover bijective through t) iff N >= 2t - 1, for every d; with prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums, the weak algebra without row sums is then free over any d <= m forms with injective column maps through t iff N >= 2t - 1. | Conjecture; exact agreement in all 25 cases checked to completion (2 <= N <= 8, 1 <= d <= 4), 3 capped cases consistent. | [Column tensor power entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-tensor-power) |
| `ex:column-tensor-power-thresholds` | Exact F_3 ranks for M = (u(W)/m^2)^(tensor N) over u(W): in all 25 cases reaching their first failure (2 <= N <= 8, 1 <= d <= 4), M is free through exactly ceil(N/2) (HF(M/mM) equals the prediction through ceil(N/2) and exceeds it at ceil(N/2)+1), independently of d; capped cases (7,4), (8,3), (8,4) free as far as checked. | Finite check; six cases recomputed independently by the reviewer. | [Column tensor power entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-column-tensor-power) |
| `prop:line-necessity` | Line necessity: over F_3, for every d >= 1 and N >= 1, the column tensor power M_N = (u(W)/m^2)^(tensor N) is not free through ceil(N/2)+1 over u(W) = F_3[W]/(w^3) (minimal-cover sense), while its restriction to every line is free through exactly ceil(N/2): freeness through t passes to restrictions to lines (Tor argument), and on a line M_N splits by the graded Clebsch-Gordan rule J_2 (x) J_2 = J_3 + J_1(-1) with summand failure degrees ceil((N+s)/2)+1. Hence the only-if half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness, also for the weak algebra without row sums over d <= m forms with injective column maps; the remaining half is a graded Dade lemma for M_N. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Line necessity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-line-necessity) |
| `prop:stability-from-tensor-power` | Stability from tensor powers: over F_p, for the weak algebra without row sums on D rows and N columns over T = F_p[R]/(R^p) (row sums), Tor_1^T(F, A~) is the Koszul homology H_1(r; A~) modulo the Frobenius classes r_i^(p-1) a e_i, so cover-freeness through t (equivalently Hilbert-function equality through t) is the statement that H_1 is spanned by Frobenius classes in degrees <= t, which is all the stability proof uses from its Step 3; hence cover-freeness through D gives no falls below D on every m >= D rows and N columns, and conj:column-tensor-power-freeness (over F_3, d = D, t = D) implies the p = 3 case of conj:weak-base-stability (N >= 2D-1). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Stability from tensor powers entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-stability-from-tensor-power) |
| `prop:tensor-power-degree-two` | Tensor powers through degree 2: over any field of characteristic != 2, the weak algebra without row sums on d rows and N >= 3 columns has only Koszul relations among its row sums in degrees <= 2 (coefficient comparison with a third column; antisymmetry; the diagonal coefficient vanishes in characteristic != 2); so over F_3 it is cover-free through 2 over F_3[R]/(R^3) for every d, and with line necessity the threshold at t = 2 is exactly N >= 3 = 2t - 1. At N = 2, a_b = x_b1 - x_b2 gives a non-Koszul relation. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Tensor power degree two entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-tensor-power-degree-two) |
| `thm:chessboard-link` | Chessboard link: over any field, on the weak algebra without row sums (d rows, N columns), the content-(1^k) strand of the Koszul complex of the row sums is, after the sign twist prod_{s in dom f} (-1)^(s-1), the augmented cochain complex of the k x N chessboard complex, so H_i(r)_(1^k) = H~^(k-i-1)(Delta_{k,N}); for every content c with prod c_b! nonzero in the field, H_i(r)_c is a retract of the multilinear strand on \|c\| rows (polarization with weights); hence H_i(r)_c = 0 for i >= 1 when N >= 2\|c\| - 1, by the chessboard connectivity bound (record's star-cover proof, ported to any field with the signed double complex). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; checked exactly over F_3 against chessboard homology for k <= 4, N <= 7. | [Chessboard link entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-chessboard-link) |
| `thm:heavy-core-reduction` | Heavy-core reduction: over F_3 with T = F_3[R]/(R^3), for a content c of the weak algebra without row sums with N >= 2\|c\| - 1, split c into heavy rows (entries >= 3, part c_H) and light rows (l cells); if Tor_1^{u(W_H)} of the heavy-row algebra on N - l columns vanishes in the pure heavy content c_H, then Tor_1^T(F_3, A~)_c = 0. Proof: change-of-rings spectral sequence for u(W_H) (x) u(W_L); polarization retract to multilinear light rows; chessboard cochains of Delta_{l,N} with coefficients in the FI-module Z_{c_H} of functions on placements of c_H with vanishing marginals; Church-Ellenberg Corollary B and Theorem A bound its generation by 2\|c_H\| and its regularity; hyperhomology over a free resolution and the chessboard bound. So conj:column-tensor-power-freeness reduces to pure heavy contents. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, using the imported Church-Ellenberg regularity theorem (statements read from the arXiv version). | [Chessboard link entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-chessboard-link) |
| `thm:one-heavy-row` | One heavy row: over F_3, Tor_1^T(F_3, A~)_c = 0 for every content c with at most one entry >= 3 and N >= 2\|c\| - 1, where A~ is the weak algebra without row sums and T = F_3[R]/(R^3): the heavy-core reduction with the pure heavy one-row case given by Clebsch-Gordan (J_2 tensor powers free through ceil(n/2)). Hence conj:column-tensor-power-freeness holds for t <= 5 and every d, and the p = 3 case of conj:weak-base-stability holds for D <= 5, N >= 2D - 1; the first uncovered content is (3,3). | Working proof after a fresh-context review; consistent with tensor_power at (N, d) = (9, 2). | [Chessboard link entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-chessboard-link) |
| `thm:tensor-power-freeness` | Tensor-power freeness: over F_3, for the weak algebra without row sums on d rows and N columns as a module over u(W) = F_3[R]/(R_b^3) through its row sums, Tor_i^{u(W)}(F_3, A~)_c = 0 for every content c and i >= 1 with N >= 2\|c\| - i. Proof: induction on the rows in the support, peeling one row by the change-of-rings spectral sequence; Clebsch-Gordan kills the terms with b >= 1, and the quotient by that row sum has a coresolution by sums of weak algebras on the other rows (dual of a free FI-resolution of the zero-marginal module, generated in degrees <= 2h+s by Church-Ellenberg), so dimension shifting uses the induction at higher Tor. Hence cover-free through t iff N >= 2t-1 for every d (conj:column-tensor-power-freeness), the p = 3 case of conj:weak-base-stability (z-injective below D for N >= 2D-1), and freeness over up to m forms with injective column maps at the same threshold. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, using the imported Church-Ellenberg regularity theorem; checked by direct Tor computations (Clebsch-Gordan and chessboard validation, contents up to (3,3) at N = 11, i <= 3). | [Tensor-power freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-tensor-power-freeness) |
| `lem:row-sum-absorption` | Row-sum absorption: over F_3, for the weak algebra without row sums A~ on m rows and N >= 2t-1 columns, with row-sum span R and forms G independent modulo R, Tor_i^{u(R+G)}(F, A~) = Tor_i^{u(G)}(F, A) in degrees <= t for all i, where A = A~/R A~ is the weak top algebra; so A~ is free through t over the row sums together with G iff A is free through t over G (change-of-rings spectral sequence and the higher-Tor vanishing of thm:tensor-power-freeness). | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [General-forms freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-general-forms-freeness) |
| `thm:general-forms-freeness` | General-forms freeness: over F_3, with g = floor(N/(2t-1)) >= 1, for every d <= m g the d-tuples of forms over which the weak algebra without row sums (m rows, N columns) is free through t form a nonempty Zariski-open set defined over F_3 with F_3-rational points (the grouped row sums over g column groups of >= 2t-1 columns, by Kunneth and thm:tensor-power-freeness; freeness restricts to sub-spans and is open, HF <= pred being equivalent to HF = pred); likewise for every e <= m(g-1) the e-tuples over which the weak top algebra A~/(row sums) is free through t (a condition on classes modulo the row sums, forcing independence). So in the stability range (m >= D) the freeness hypothesis of prop:one-count-by-freeness holds on a nonempty open set of inventories, generic over F_3bar, whenever 1 <= nh <= m(floor(N/(2D-1)) - 1); it does not place a given F_3-rational inventory in that set. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; grouped configurations checked exactly at seven sizes; random F_3 forms usually exceed the theorem's count. | [General-forms freeness entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-general-forms-freeness) |
| `cor:ens-members` | ENS members: over F_3, on the weak unary base with m >= D rows and N >= 2D-1 columns, any family of complete accuracy-one ENS selector blocks (affine inputs L, q = 1 - L^2, private coefficients r with r^3 = r, companions q_i P with P = 1 - sum r_i q_i) whose input forms' linear parts are linearly independent modulo the row sums, with the weak top algebra free through D over their span, is z-injective below D and has no PC refutation of degree D (content for m > N and D >= 5). The family is one member with private variables over the base extended by the field equations of r: base stability passes through a tensor product with a free F[z]-module, freeness passes to A tensor F[r]/(r^3), span transfer applies with r among the forms, each block is satisfiable at every point, and relative gluing with one member needs no splitting. No conservativity is used; it removes the ENS gap of prop:one-count-by-freeness under that proposition's own hypotheses, which by thm:general-forms-freeness hold at the F_3-rational points of a nonempty open set of families of up to m(floor(N/(2D-1))-1) forms; whether a given random F_3 inventory lies there stays open. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; the record check found it new. | [ENS members entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-ens-members) |
| `prop:one-count-composition` | One-count composition: over F_3 at D = 11 on the top-size lemma's calibration inventory, (1) the one-count instance the lemma requires (n tuples at h in [Q(L_max - 1), Q(L_max)), Q(L) ~ 1.6e4 L Lambda_M) fits the proved range of cor:ens-members with thm:general-forms-freeness (about n^2/21 forms on the full board) exactly when L_max <~ n/(3.4e5 Lambda_M), so a design exists there for inventories in the free set (for the random inventory conditional on lying there, and the reduction under (T)); this is bare existence, not a design in the endpoint span the lemma uses; (2) at every residual size L the band blocks carry about n Q(L)^2/2 forms, about 1.3e8 n Lambda_M^2 times the independence bound dim A_1(L) ~ L^2 of a single glued member, so glued components handle a vanishing fraction of each size's band. | Working composition after a fresh-context review; arithmetic from the recorded thresholds. | [Mixture composition entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-mixture-composition) |
| `thm:planted-falls-degree-two` | Planted falls at degree 2: over F_3, on the homogenized weak base B with z injective in degrees 0 and 1 (m >= 2, N >= 3), with m <= N so that a matching exists, adding M selectors s_t = 1 - (L_t - v_t)^2 gives dim ker(z: B'_1 -> B'_2) = rank{s_t^h} - rank{l_t^2} (tops in A_2); planted selectors (L_t - v_t nonzero at the matching) lie in and span the hyperplane H = ker(ev) of B_2, of dimension tau_2 + gamma_1 (tau_2 = dim A_2, gamma_1 = dim A_1), so for planted families parametrized by u_t in z + K and in general position (a nonempty Zariski-open condition with F_3-rational points) dim ker z_1 = min(gamma_1, max(0, M - tau_2)): the planted part of conj:planted-excess-falls for families in general position (the random-valued clause is not proved), matching every recorded value. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; agrees with every recorded run of ex:planted-excess-falls-check. | [Planted falls proof entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-planted-falls-proof) |
| `cor:ens-span-members` | ENS members over a free span: cor:ens-members holds without independence of the input forms; if the weak top algebra is free through D over the span W of the linear parts of all input forms (with the other hypotheses of cor:ens-members: over F_3, m >= D, N >= 2D-1, content for D >= 5), the weak base plus any family of complete accuracy-one ENS blocks has no PC refutation of degree D, by thm:generic-span-members (dependent forms of the span allowed) with the blocks' private coefficients. So the capacity limit is on dim W, not on the number of forms. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Planted falls proof entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-planted-falls-proof) |
| `prop:free-span-double-points` | Free-span double points: over F_3, on the weak base with m >= 3 rows and N >= 5 columns, for M selectors 1-(L_t - v_t)^2 (any values) whose linear parts lie in a span W of dimension d >= 2 over which the weak top algebra G is free through 3, the conditions of thm:glued-double-points taken in G (squares independent in G_2; dim sum l_t^2 G_1 = M(gamma_1 - 1)) are equivalent to the single condition (b') that Phi: W^M -> T_3, (w_t) -> sum l_t^2 w_t, has rank M(d-1) in T = F_3[W]/(w^3), which also implies independence of the squares; under it the top syzygies through 3 are Frobenius only and thm:based-taylor-glue gives no PC refutation of degree 3 for F_3-rational forms and values. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Free-span double points entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-free-span-double-points) |
| `prop:truncated-double-points-small` | Truncated double points for small d: for every 4 <= d <= 24, generic linear forms in T = F_3[y_1..y_d]/(y_i^3) have independent squares in T_2 and double-point map Phi: W^M -> T_3 of rank min(M(d-1), dim T_3) for every M, dim T_3 = C(d+2,3) - d; proved by one exact F_3 witness per d at M_inj = floor(dim T_3/(d-1)) and M_inj + 1, lower semicontinuity of rank, and the prefix argument. | Working proof by exact computation after a fresh-context review; the near-square cases d = 6, 7, 24 needed more seeds. | [Free-span double points entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-free-span-double-points) |

With prop:free-span-double-points and thm:general-forms-freeness it gives no degree-3 refutation for about d^2/6 selectors generic in a common free span (N >= 10 for d >= 4) of dimension up to m(floor(N/5) - 1). | Conjecture; proved for 4 <= d <= 24 (prop:truncated-double-points-small). | [Free-span double points entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-free-span-double-points) |
| `lem:horace-residual-defect` | Horace residual defect: for double points in T = F_3[y_1..y_d]/(y_i^3), degree 3, the hyperplane split T_3 = T'_3 + T'_2 y_d + T'_1 y_d^2 gives rank Phi >= rank(trace) + rank(residual), with exact dimension split (d-1)(d+2)/2; for r <= d-1 unspecialized forms l' + y_d with independent l', the residual map has kernel of dimension at least r + C(r-1,2) (Frobenius and the Koszul combinations whose T'_1 parts cancel among the r-1 dimensional span of differences), so for every split the inequality trace + residual certifies maximal rank only when r <= 2 (about two new forms per dimension), although the specialized configuration itself can exceed the inequality; best-of-5-seeds GF(3) ranks for 6 <= d <= 40 at the balanced split equal min(target, s + r(d-1) - C(r-1,2)) except d = 8 (one lower, unexplained). | Working proof of the lower bound after a fresh-context review; equality is a finite check. | [Horace residual defect entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-horace-residual-defect) |
| `prop:board-double-points-from-free-spans` | Board double points from free spans: over F_3, on the weak base with m >= 3 rows and N >= 10 columns, if 4 <= d <= m(floor(N/5)-1) and the truncated double-point property holds at d with an exact F_3 witness (certified for 4 <= d <= 24 and d = 28, 32, 36), then for every M <= floor((C(d+2,3)-d)/(d-1)) the M-tuples of board linear forms satisfying (a) and (b) of thm:glued-double-points in the weak top algebra form a nonempty Zariski-open set with F_3-rational points (the witness inside an F_3-rational free span from grouped row sums), and selectors whose forms are an F_3-rational point of it have no degree-3 PC refutation for any values (thm:glued-double-points, weak balanced version). | `lem:ens-block-span-fall` | ENS block span fall: over F_3, a complete accuracy-one ENS block with two inputs (q_i = 1 - L_i^2, P = 1 - r_1 q_1 - r_2 q_2, companions q_i P) has a fall in its span ring: zR is a nonzero degree-5 element killed by z, where L_2 q_1 (1 - r_1) R = L_2 q_1 (1 - r_1) is the degree-4 consequence with z^2 R in the homogenized ideal (from L_2 c_1 = L_2 q_1(1-r_1) - r_2 q_1 (L_2 q_2)). | `check:per-order-base-dimension-through-16` | For 1 <= k <= 16 and 0 <= l < k, delta(m(k),k,l) = m(k)+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1) with m(k) = floor(log2 k)+2: 136 exact values, 81 of them at orders not settled by earlier results, zero mismatches. | Finite check by the jet kernel research/tools/bmd_jet_orders.cpp, validated against all 24 cases of the dense exact table with zero mismatches. | [Per-order formula through k = 16](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-base-dimension) |

| `conj:binary-multiplicity-per-order-formula` | For every k >= 1, 0 <= l < k and n >= floor(log2 k)+2, the least degree of an F_2 polynomial with Hasse multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is n+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1). | Proved by thm:per-order-value-small-multiplicity (additive polynomials on the span of y_1..y_n). | [Per-order formula through k = 16](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-base-dimension), [proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-additive-roots) |
| `conj:binary-multiplicity-per-order-all-dimensions` | For all n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree of an F_2 polynomial in n variables with Hasse multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j); equivalently delta(n,c,0) = c + delta(n-1,ceil(c/2),0) and delta(n,k,l) = 2l + delta(n,k-l,0). | Proved by thm:per-order-value-all-dimensions (reduction modulo the subspace polynomial of the span of y_1..y_n). | [All-dimension per-order formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-all-dimension-formula), [proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-subspace-reduction) |
| `lem:per-order-all-dimension-minimum` | With Phi(n,k,l) = n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j): Phi = n+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1) when k-l-1 < 2^n, and min over l of Phi equals 2k+n-2-floor(log2 k) for k < 2^(n-1) and 2k - floor(k/2^(n-1)) for k >= 2^(n-1). | Working proof: Legendre's formula reduces Phi to n+2k-2-(2q+s_2(r)); maximizing 2q+s_2(r) by cases. | [All-dimension per-order formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-all-dimension-formula), [Lean: the digit argument](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-lean-preprint-side-claims) |
| `check:per-order-all-dimension-values` | All 696 exact per-order minima for n <= 5, k <= 16 and (n,k) = (6,16) equal n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j); the halving law holds on all 81 order-zero values and the exchange law on 681 values. | Finite check by the validated jet kernel bmd_jet_orders and bmd_halving_check.py; zero mismatches. | [All-dimension per-order formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-all-dimension-formula) |
| `thm:per-order-all-dimension-upper-bound` | For n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, with c-1 = k-l-1 = q 2^n + r (0 <= r < 2^n), the polynomial y_1^l F^(2q) g_(r+1), F the product of all 2^n-1 affine hyperplane forms 1+u.x and g_s the truncated product, has multiplicity >= k at nonzero points of F_2^n, exactly l at the origin, and degree <= n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j). | Working proof: composition of the hyperplane product (mult >= 2^(n-1), value 1 at 0), the truncated product and y_1^l, all verified in Lean; degree by Legendre's formula. | [All-dimension upper bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-all-dimension-upper-bound) |
| `lem:hyperplane-restriction-dichotomy` | If P over F_2 in n variables has Hasse multiplicity >= k at all nonzero points and exactly l < k at the origin, then deg P >= 2k or P = F P' with F the product of the 2^n-1 affine forms 1+u.x, P' of multiplicity >= k-2^(n-1) at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin; so delta(n,c,0) >= min(2c, 2^n-1+delta(n,c-2^(n-1),0)). | Working proof: restriction to each origin-avoiding hyperplane lies in (y)^k of the hyperplane (origin-jet lemma), so it is 0 or of degree >= 2k. | [Hyperplane dichotomy](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-hyperplane-dichotomy) |
| `thm:order-zero-value-small-dimensions` | For 1 <= n <= 3 and every c >= 1, the least degree of an F_2 polynomial in n variables with P(0) != 0 and Hasse multiplicity >= c at all nonzero points is n + sum_{j<n} floor((c-1)/2^j). | Working proof: upper bound from thm:per-order-all-dimension-upper-bound; lower bound by the one-dimension step and the hyperplane dichotomy, matched by exact identities of Phi. | [Hyperplane dichotomy](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-hyperplane-dichotomy) |
| `lem:y-coefficient-degree-formula` | With x(Y) = sum_t Y^(2^t) and w = v(x(y_1),...,x(y_n)), the coefficient of x^eps y^e (\|e\| < k) in the polynomial P(v) of an origin jet v is the y^e-coefficient of w prod_{i: eps_i=0}(1+x(y_i)); so deg P(v) = max of n-\|S\|+2\|e\| over S and \|e\| < k with nonzero y^e-coefficient of w u^S. | Working proof: the two roots x(y), 1+x(y) of X^2+X=y separate the y-basis coefficients; checked on 240 random jets. | [Per-order formula proved](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-additive-roots) |
| `thm:per-order-value-small-multiplicity` | For n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k with k-l <= 2^n, the least degree of an F_2 polynomial in n variables with Hasse multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is n+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1); in particular for every n >= floor(log2 k)+2. | Working proof: degree conditions make multi-additive forms E_j vanish on the 2^n-element F_2-span of y_1..y_n; their degree is < 2^n, so they vanish identically, forcing the order-l part of the jet to be 0. | [Per-order formula proved](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-additive-roots) |
| `cor:per-order-all-dimensions-small-n` | For 1 <= n <= 4 and all 0 <= l < k, delta(n,k,l) = n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j). | Working proof: the additive-roots theorem for k-l <= 2^n and the hyperplane dichotomy above it. | [Per-order formula proved](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-additive-roots) |
| `thm:per-order-value-all-dimensions` | For all n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree of an F_2 polynomial in n variables with Hasse multiplicity >= k at every nonzero point and exactly l at the origin is n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j). | Working proof: degree conditions at \|e\| = k-1-t couple multi-additive forms through a repeated-argument recursion, so they vanish on the span V of y_1..y_n; reduction modulo the subspace polynomial of V isolates the order-l part of the jet. Upper bound by y_1^l F^(2q) g_(r+1). | [Per-order minimum in every dimension](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-subspace-reduction) |
| `check:q-ary-per-order-values` | All 149 exact per-order minima on the full grid F_q^n for q=3 (n <= 3, k <= 8) and q=5 (n <= 2, k <= 7) equal n(q-1) + q l + (q-1) sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/q^j). | Finite check by the prime-field jet kernel bmd_jet_orders_q, validated on binary values and the recorded high-origin and first-jet results. | [Per-order law on F_q grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-q-ary-scoping) |
| `conj:q-ary-per-order-formula` | For every prime q, n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree of P over F_q with Hasse multiplicity >= k at every nonzero point of F_q^n and exactly l at the origin is n(q-1) + q l + (q-1) sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/q^j). | Proved by thm:q-ary-per-order-value, for every prime power q. | [Per-order law on F_q grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-q-ary-scoping), [proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-q-ary-proof) |
| `lem:q-ary-coefficient-formula` | Over F_q with y_i = x_i^q - x_i and x(y) = -sum_t y^(q^t), the coefficient of x^eps y^e (\|e\| < k) in the admissible polynomial of an origin jet v is the y^e-coefficient of w prod_i gamma_(eps_i)(x(y_i)), w = v(x(y)), gamma_eps the X^eps-coefficient of 1-(X-x)^(q-1). | Working proof: Lagrange interpolation over the q roots x(y)+a of X^q - X = y. | [Per-order minimum on F_q grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-q-ary-proof) |
| `thm:q-ary-per-order-value` | For every prime power q, n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree of P over F_q with Hasse multiplicity >= k at every nonzero point of F_q^n and exactly l at the origin is n(q-1) + q l + (q-1) sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/q^j). | Working proof: construction (x_1^q-x_1)^l F^(qQ) P(1); lower bound by F_q-multilinear forms vanishing on the q^n-element span, multinomial vanishing mod p, and reduction modulo the subspace q-polynomial. | [Per-order minimum on F_q grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-q-ary-proof) |
| `check:odd-cube-per-order-values` | Exact per-order minima on the cube {0,1}^n over F_3 (n <= 5, k <= 13) and F_5 (n <= 5, k <= 12): all 100 values with n >= k-1 agree with Menezes' n+2k-2-rho_F(k-l); below his range the values fall under that expression. | Finite check by bmd_jet_orders_q --cube, validated against Menezes' theorem and earlier binary and full-grid data. | [Cube over odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-odd-cube-scoping) |
| `ex:odd-cube-exchange-law-failure` | Over F_3 and F_5 on the cube, delta(3,12,3) = 22 < 2*3 + delta(3,9,0) = 23, so the binary exchange law delta(n,k,l) = 2l + delta(n,k-l,0) fails in odd characteristic. | Refutation by exact computation (bmd_jet_orders_q --cube). | [Cube over odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-odd-cube-scoping) |
| `conj:cube-square-per-order-any-field` | For every field F and 0 <= l < k, the least degree on {0,1}^2 with order >= k at the three nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is 2k - ceil((k-l-1)/2). | Proved by thm:cube-square-per-order-any-field. | [Cube over odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-odd-cube-scoping), [proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-square-all-orders) |
| `thm:cube-square-order-zero-any-field` | For every field F and c >= 1, the least degree of P in F[x_1,x_2] with P(0) != 0 and multiplicity >= c at (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) is 2c - ceil((c-1)/2). | Working proof: powers of G=(1-x_1)(1-x_2)(1-x_1-x_2); lower bound by the line dichotomy and the step P(t,1)-P(t,0). | [Square over every field; polynomial relaxation for covers](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-square-and-cover-limit) |
| `cor:polynomial-relaxation-value-for-covers` | For every prime power q and n,k >= 1, the least degree of a polynomial over F_q with multiplicity >= k on F_q^n minus 0 and < k at 0 is D_q(n,k) = n(q-1)+q(k-1)-max_{m<=k-1}(q floor(m/q^n)+s_q(m mod q^n)); it is a lower bound for f_q(n,k,1) and the best one available from value and multiplicity conditions alone; for k <= q it equals n(q-1)+(q-1)(k-1). | Working proof: minimization of thm:q-ary-per-order-value over the origin order. | [Square over every field; polynomial relaxation for covers](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-square-and-cover-limit) |
| `thm:cube-square-per-order-any-field` | For every field F and 0 <= l < k, the least degree of P in F[x_1,x_2] with multiplicity >= k at (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) and exactly l at the origin is 2k - ceil((k-l-1)/2). | Working proof: the line dichotomy reduces to k-l-1 in {0,1}; those base cases follow from the origin-jet lemma over any field; upper bound y_1^l times the order-zero construction. | [The square over every field, every order](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-square-all-orders) |
| `ex:subspace-grid-base-law-failure` | On grids S^n with S = {0,1,a,1+a} in GF(8) (a^3 = a+1), n = 2, k = 5, the exact-origin-order minima for l = 0..4 are 20,20,21,21,22, not the base-s values 21,19,20,21,22; the base-s law also fails on every other tested F_2-subspace that is not a scaled subfield. | Refutation by exact computation (bmd_jet_orders_gf), checked by an independent brute force; scaled subfields satisfy the law by the q-ary theorem. | [Additive-subgroup grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-subspace-grids) |
| `conj:four-element-subspace-square-law` | For a 4-element F_2-subspace S of GF(2^a) that is not a scaled F_4 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree on S^2 with multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is 6+4(k-1)-2 floor(m/8)-ceil((m mod 8)/2), m = k-l-1. | Proved by thm:four-element-square-law (root-curve count and the upper half). | [Additive-subgroup grids](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-subspace-grids) |
| `lem:subspace-grid-coefficient-formula` | For an F_2-subspace S of a characteristic-2 field with L = prod_{t in S}(x-t), y_i = L(x_i) and additive root x(y), the coefficient of x^eps y^e (\|e\| < k) in the admissible polynomial of an origin jet v is the y^e-coefficient of w prod_i Lambda_{eps_i}(x(y_i)), w = v(x(y)), Lambda_eps the X^eps-coefficient of L(X+x)/(c_0 (X+x)). | Working proof: Lagrange interpolation over the nodes x(y)+t, whose differences are nonzero constants. | [Subspace grids: a nonzero second coefficient](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-second-coefficient) |
| `thm:second-coefficient-savings` | If S is an F_2-subspace of a characteristic-2 field with \|S\| = s >= 4 and the x^2 coefficient of prod_{t in S}(x-t) is nonzero, then for n >= 2 and k >= 3 the least degree with multiplicity >= k at the nonzero points of S^n and exactly k-3 at the origin is n(s-1)+s(k-1)-1, one more than the base-s law. | Working proof: the conditions from the terms with one entry of eps lowered, at \|e\| = k-1, force a_1 (y_1 - y_2) w_{k-3} = 0; upper bound from the jet L(x_1)^{k-3}. | [Subspace grids: a nonzero second coefficient](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-second-coefficient) |
| `thm:four-element-base-block` | For a four-element F_2-subspace S of a characteristic-2 field that is not a scaled F_4, and 0 <= l < k with m = k-l-1 <= 7, the least degree on S^2 with multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is 6+4(k-1)-ceil(m/2). | Working proof by exact certificates over F_2[B,y1,y2] (Singular, checked by an independent Python expansion): an attaining syzygy with top component 1 and a B-free annihilator of the top component. | [Four-element square law: the base block and the upper half](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-four-element-base-block) |
| `thm:four-element-upper-half` | For a four-element F_2-subspace S of a characteristic-2 field that is not a scaled F_4 and all 0 <= l < k, the least degree on S^2 with multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is at most 6+4(k-1)-2 floor(m/8)-ceil((m mod 8)/2), m = k-l-1. | Working proof: products L(x_1)^l Q and Q_c Q_8 reduce to the order-zero values for c <= 8 given by the base block. | [Four-element square law: the base block and the upper half](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-four-element-base-block) |
| `lem:root-curve-orders` | For an F_2-subspace S (\|S\| = s) of a characteristic-2 field, z_i = x(y_i T) with L(z_i) = y_i T, and Ord(d) the T-orders of K-combinations of z_1^a z_2^b (a+b <= d, K = F(y1,y2)): savings >= h at m on S^2 forces m not in Ord(h-1), and \|Ord(d)\| = C(d+2,2) - C(d+2-s,2). | Working proof: the coefficient conditions are a functional supported on T^0..T^m killing low-degree monomials in z; the kernel of Z -> z is generated by the irreducible y2 L(Z1) + y1 L(Z2). | [The four-element square law is a theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-four-element-square-theorem) |
| `thm:four-element-square-law` | For a four-element F_2-subspace S of a characteristic-2 field that is not a scaled F_4 and all 0 <= l < k, the least degree on S^2 with multiplicity >= k at nonzero points and exactly l at the origin is 6+4(k-1)-2 floor(m/8)-ceil((m mod 8)/2), m = k-l-1. | Working proof: the upper half gives Ord(d) inside {H <= d}; the root-curve count shows both have 4d-2 elements (d >= 3), so they are equal, which gives the lower bound. | [The four-element square law is a theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-four-element-square-theorem) |
| `lem:root-curve-independence` | For an F_2-subspace S (\|S\| = s) of a characteristic-2 field and z_i = x(y_i T), i <= n: savings >= h at m on S^n forces m not in Ord(h-1); and the T^Q z^r (r in [0,s-1]^n) are independent over F(y), so \|Ord(d)\| >= N_{s,n}(d) = #{(Q,r): sQ+\|r\| <= d}. | Working proof: the two-variable functional argument in n variables; linear disjointness of the extensions L(Z) = y_j T by a degree argument in y_j. | [The counting principle](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-counting-principle) |
| `thm:root-curve-counting-principle` | On a grid S^n (S an F_2-subspace, \|S\| = s, characteristic 2), if savings H(m) are attained for every m = k-l-1 and #{m : H(m) <= d} = N_{s,n}(d) for all d, then every polynomial with multiplicity >= k off the origin and order exactly l at it has savings <= H(m): delta_S(n,k,l) >= n(s-1)+s(k-1)-H(m). | Working proof: attained savings put Ord(d) inside {H <= d}; independence gives \|Ord(d)\| >= N(d); equal sizes force equality, and the functional gives the bound. | [The counting principle](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-counting-principle) |
| `cor:root-curve-lower-bounds` | The counting principle reproves the lower bounds of the binary all-dimension per-order theorem, the q-ary theorem for q = 2^delta, and the four-element square theorem (c_1 != 0), by digit bijections and a generating-function identity. | Working proof: condition (1) is each recorded construction; condition (2) is the base-q digit bijection or (1+t+t^2+t^3)^2/(1-t^4) = (1+t+t^2+t^3)/(1-t). | [The counting principle](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-counting-principle) |
| `lem:root-curve-sharpness` | For every F_2-subspace S (\|S\| = s) of a characteristic-2 field and n >= 1, the root curve z_i = x(y_i T) has exactly N_{s,n}(d) = #{(Q,r) in N x [0,s-1]^n : sQ+\|r\| <= d} distinct T-orders among polynomials of degree <= d in z. | Working proof: >= by linear disjointness; <= by reducing monomials with y1 L(Z_i) + y_i L(Z_1) to Z_1^{sQ} Z^r. | [The stable per-order law on every additive grid](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-stable-per-order-law) |
| `thm:stable-per-order-law` | On every additive grid S^n (characteristic 2), the per-order savings h(k,l) at m = k-l-1 are at most kappa(m) = least degree of a polynomial in the root curve z_i = x(y_i T) with T-order exactly m, do not decrease in l, and equal kappa(m) for all large l; #{m : kappa(m) <= d} = N_{s,n}(d). | Working proof: lemma (a) for the bound; a K-linear functional killing low-degree z-monomials, cleared of denominators and cut to one homogeneous component, gives a jet for large l; sharpness gives the count. | [The stable per-order law on every additive grid](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-stable-per-order-law) |
| `thm:root-curve-theory-char-p` | For an F_p-subspace S (\|S\| = s = p^sigma) of a characteristic-p field and n >= 1: the subspace coefficient formula, the root-curve bound (savings h at m force m not in Ord(h-1)), the exact count \|Ord(d)\| = N_{s,n}(d), the counting principle and the stable per-order law (savings <= kappa(m), equal for large l) all hold. | Working proof: the characteristic-2 proofs carry over with the Lagrange constant prod(-t), Lucas for binom(s-1,a) mod p, and signs in the reductions. | [The root-curve theory in every characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-root-curve-char-p) |
| `cor:q-ary-counting-proof` | For every prime power q, the lower bound of the q-ary per-order theorem on F_q^n follows from its construction by the counting principle (digit bijection m -> (Q, base-q digits of r)). | Working proof: the q-ary construction attains savings qQ + s_q(r) for every l; the digit bijection gives the count N_{q,n}. | [The root-curve theory in every characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-root-curve-char-p) |
| `thm:finite-grid-stable-law` | For every field, every finite S containing 0 (\|S\| = s), L = prod_{t in S}(x-t), r_0 the root of L(X) = y at 0 and z_i = r_0(y_i T): on S^n the per-order savings at m = k-l-1 are at most kappa(m) (least degree of a polynomial in z with T-order m), nondecreasing in l, equal to kappa(m) for large l, and #{m : kappa(m) <= d} = N_{s,n}(d). | Working proof: the additive-case root-curve proofs with Hensel roots as Lagrange nodes, the unit L'(r_0) absorbed into the jet, and independence by Gauss's lemma (L(Z) - y_j T is linear in y_j). | [The stable per-order law on every finite grid](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-finite-grid-stable-law) |
| `lem:catalan-linear-forms` | On the cube root curve z_i = r_0(y_i T), r_0 the root of X^2 - X = y at 0, a K-linear form in z_1..z_n has T-order exactly a whenever C_{a-1} != 0 in F and at most n of C_0..C_{a-1} are nonzero; products give kappa_n(m) <= rho_{F,<=n}(m+1). | Working proof: the T^j coefficient of sum beta_i z_i is (-1)^j C_{j-1} sum beta_i y_i^j; a generalized Vandermonde solves the conditions at the nonzero-Catalan exponents. | [The cube over every field: a capped Catalan lower bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-capped-catalan) |
| `thm:cube-capped-catalan-bound` | For every field F, n >= 1 and 0 <= l < k, the least degree on {0,1}^n with multiplicity >= k off the origin and exactly l at it is at least n+2(k-1)-rho_{F,<=n}(k-l) (fewest n-allowed Catalan parts); for n >= k-l-1 this is Menezes' n+2k-2-rho_F(k-l), and over F_2 it is the binary per-order law. | Working proof: savings <= kappa_n(m) by the finite-grid stable law, and kappa_n(m) <= rho_{F,<=n}(m+1) by Catalan linear forms. | [The cube over every field: a capped Catalan lower bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-capped-catalan) |
| `cor:menezes-range-extension` | If Menezes' order-zero construction delta_F(n,c,0) <= n+2c-2-rho_F(c) (n >= c-1) holds, then delta_F(n,k,l) = n+2k-2-rho_F(k-l) for all n >= k-l-1, not only n >= k-1. | Now unconditional: thm:catalan-truncation-any-field proves the needed construction over every field and dimension (thm:cube-catalan-sandwich). | [The cube over every field: a capped Catalan lower bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-capped-catalan) |
| `thm:catalan-truncation-any-field` | Over every field and for all n, the truncation g_s of prod_i N_s(x_i), N_s = (x-1) - sum_{a<s} (-1)^(a-1) C_{a-1} (x^2-x)^a, has multiplicity >= s at nonzero points of {0,1}^n, g_s(0) = (-1)^n and degree <= n+2s-2-rho_F(s); so y_1^l g_{k-l} gives delta_F(n,k,l) <= n+2k-2-rho_F(k-l). | Working proof: N_s vanishes to order s at 1 because x-1 is the Catalan series in y; truncated terms have multiplicity >= s; the degree bound uses monotonicity of 2 sigma - rho_F(sigma+1). Exact checks over F_3, F_5, F_7 with a negative control. | [The Catalan sandwich](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-catalan-sandwich) |
| `thm:cube-catalan-sandwich` | On {0,1}^n over every field, the per-order savings n+2(k-1)-delta_F(n,k,l) lie between rho_F(k-l) and kappa_n(k-l-1) <= rho_{F,<=n}(k-l); hence delta_F(n,k,l) = n+2k-2-rho_F(k-l) for all n >= k-l-1. | Working proof: upper bound from the Catalan truncation, lower bound from the capped Catalan bound; they agree for n >= k-l-1. | [The Catalan sandwich](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-catalan-sandwich) |
| `lem:cube-degree-one-orders` | On the cube's Catalan root curve over a field F, the T-orders of affine forms in z_1..z_n are exactly 0 and the n-allowed parts (C_{a-1} != 0 and at most n of C_0..C_{a-1} nonzero); they are {0,...,n} iff C_0..C_{n-1} are nonzero in F. | Working proof: linear-form lemma for the allowed parts; a generalized Vandermonde forces beta = 0 when more than n conditions apply. | [The cube's stable orders form initial segments](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-initial-segment) |
| `conj:cube-initial-segment-law` | If the Catalan numbers C_0..C_{n-1} are nonzero in F (e.g. characteristic 0), the root-curve orders of degree <= d on the cube form {0,...,N_{2,n}(d)-1}, so the stable per-order savings are kappa_n(m) = min{d : N_{2,n}(d) > m}, N_{2,n} the partial sums of (1+t)^n/(1-t^2). | Conjecture: proved for d <= 1 and n <= 2; matches a majority of random specializations in all 13 computed cases with the hypothesis (F_3..F_13, n <= 5; deviating trials only in F_121, F_169, and reruns in F_13 and F_1331 match 6 of 6), fails in both computed cases without it. | [The cube's stable orders form initial segments](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-initial-segment) |
| `lem:cube-order-determinant` | For the cube's Catalan root curve, the orders of polynomials of degree <= d form {0,...,N_{2,n}(d)-1} over F iff an explicit integer determinant Delta_{n,d}(y) (coefficients of T^1..T^{N-1} in the basis T^Q z^r) is nonzero in F[y]; one specialization with initial orders certifies this in characteristic p and in characteristic 0. | Working proof: the sharpness basis, orders = {0} union orders of the non-constant part, injectivity of truncation; specialization preserves the spanning identities when y_1 != 0. | [The cube's order determinant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-determinant) |
| `check:cube-initial-segment-certificates` | Exact determinants: Delta_{3,2}, Delta_{3,3}, Delta_{3,4}, Delta_{4,2} have integer contents 4, 2, 8, 8 (powers of 2), so the initial-segment law holds there in every odd characteristic and in characteristic 0; trial certificates add n = 4 (d <= 3) and n = 5 (d <= 2) in characteristic 0. | Finite check by Singular determinants and factorization, and by specialization certificates from the recorded trials. | [The cube's order determinant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-determinant) |
| `conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law` | In characteristic != 2, the cube's root-curve orders satisfy Ord_n(1) = {0} union the n-allowed Catalan parts and Ord_n(d) = {0,...,N_{2,n}(d)-1} for all d >= 2; equivalently content(Delta_{n,d}) is a power of 2 for d >= 2. | Conjecture: proved in characteristic 0 for all n, d, for n <= 3 in every characteristic != 2, for p > 2^{n-1} d in general, and in every odd characteristic for n = 4 (2 <= d <= 6), 5 (2 <= d <= 4), 6 (2 <= d <= 3); open for the odd primes <= 2^{n-1} d beyond these cases. | [The cube's order determinant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-determinant) |
| `lem:cube-hermite-pade-form` | In characteristic != 2, with w_i = 1 - 2z_i = (1+4y_iT)^{1/2}, the cube's root-curve polynomials of degree <= d are the direct sum of w^r F(y)[T]_{<= floor((d-\|r\|)/2)}; the initial-segment law at (n,d) is normality of this type I Hermite-Pade multi-index for the products of square roots, and the w-determinant is +-2^e Delta_{n,d}. | Working proof: w_i^2 = 1+4y_iT, and a unitriangular-up-to-powers-of-2 change of the sharpness basis. | [The cube's order determinant as a Hermite–Padé normality problem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-hermite-pade) |
| `check:cube-determinant-certificates-many-primes` | Delta_{n,d} is nonzero modulo every odd prime p <= 67 for the 32 pairs with 2 <= n <= 6, 2 <= d <= 12 and N_{2,n}(d) <= 50, and modulo every odd p <= 89 for 2 <= n <= 6, 2 <= d <= 3 (extension recorded 25 September in the large-characteristic entry); with thm:cube-large-characteristic this gives the refined law in every odd characteristic for n = 4 (2 <= d <= 6), 5 (2 <= d <= 4), 6 (2 <= d <= 3). Lex-extremal coefficients (-4, 6, -8008) do not bound the content. | Finite check by random evaluation over GF(p^a), p^a >= 300, with a p = 2 negative control that fails exactly for n >= 3. | [The cube's order determinant as a Hermite–Padé normality problem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-hermite-pade) |
| `lem:cube-curve-transport` | On the curve C_a: w_i^2 = 1 + a_i T (char != 2, a_i distinct nonzero), polynomials of degree <= d in w have basis T^Q w^r; rescaling at any unramified point q gives the Hermite-Pade problem at a'_i = a_i / w_i(q)^2, so Delta_{n,d} is nonzero mod p iff the series V_d has orders 0..N-1 at some point (V_d classical). | Working proof: Kummer independence, rescaling of the square roots, and the w-determinant of the Hermite-Pade form. | [The cube's orders on a curve](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-curve-orders) |
| `thm:cube-initial-segment-char-zero` | Delta_{n,d} != 0 in Z[y] for all n, d >= 1: over every field of characteristic 0 the cube's root-curve orders of degree <= d are {0,...,N_{2,n}(d)-1}, kappa_n(m) = min{d : N_{2,n}(d) > m}, and the real cube's stable per-order savings equal this kappa. | Working proof: the Wronskian of the basis is a nonzero rational function on C_a, so a general point has standard orders; the transport lemma moves it to p0. | [The cube's orders on a curve](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-curve-orders) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-law` | Over every field of characteristic != 2, Ord_3(d) = {0,...,4d-1} for every d >= 1 (content(Delta_{3,d}) is a power of 2): C_a is a genus-1 curve, the law at d fails iff d*2c_1 = 0, and c_1 maps to -2P_0 on Y^2 = prod(1+a_iT), which has infinite order by specialization to the generic point of a constant elliptic curve. | Working proof: Riemann-Hurwitz, Riemann-Roch, sign involutions as x -> -x + c_i, an isogeny, and a spreading-out argument. | [The cube's orders on a curve](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-curve-orders) |
| `check:cube-elliptic-orders` | For 56 random specializations a in F_p^3 (p = 5..23), the first failing degree of Delta_{3,d}(a/4) is o' or 2o' with o' = ord(4P_0) on Y^2 = prod(1+a_iT), as the torsion criterion predicts; both alternatives occur. | Finite check by direct determinant evaluation and brute-force point orders. | [The cube's orders on a curve](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-curve-orders) |
| `lem:cube-binomial-order-criterion` | If some point P of C_a unramified over T has V_d-orders j_0 < ... < j_{N-1} with prod(j_l' - j_l)/prod_{i<N} i! prime to p (odd), then p does not divide content(Delta_{n,d}) (Stohr-Voloch's binomial criterion via the Hasse Wronskian, plus the transport lemma). | Working proof following Torres's exposition (arXiv math/0011091, Lemma 2.7) of Stohr-Voloch 1986; Hasse derivatives on F(C_a) agree with Taylor coefficients at unramified points. | [The cube's initial-segment law for p above the degree](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-large-characteristic) |
| `thm:cube-large-characteristic` | For all n, d and every odd prime p > 2^{n-1} d, p does not divide content(Delta_{n,d}): the cube's degree-<=d root-curve orders are {0,...,N_{2,n}(d)-1} in characteristic p, and each (n,d) case of the refined law is a finite check over the odd primes <= 2^{n-1} d. | Working proof: orders of V_d are at most its pole degree 2^{n-1} d, so the binomial criterion applies at p0. | [The cube's initial-segment law for p above the degree](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-large-characteristic) |
| `ex:cube-one-step-lag-fails` | On {0,1}^3 over F_101 and F_3, the savings at m = 28 are 6 for l = 0, 1 (and l = 2 over F_3) while kappa_3(28) = 8: the pre-stable savings can lag kappa by 2, refuting kappa - 1 <= h at every l; at l = 0 the savings grow with period 5 against period 4 for kappa. | Refutation by exact kernel values (bmd_jet_orders_q --cube) for k <= 30 over F_101 and k <= 32 over F_3, compared with the proved kappa_3. | [Pre-stable savings on the cube](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-threshold-ideal) |
| `lem:cube-threshold-ideal` | On the cube over any field, the savings satisfy h(k,l) >= h iff the homogeneous ideal I^{(h)}_m (last coordinates of solutions of the root-curve condition system) has a nonzero element of degree l; so h(k,l) = max{h : indeg I^{(h)}_m <= l}. At the kappa-boundary m = N_{2,n}(h-1) with initial Ord(h-1), the solutions are free of rank 1 and the threshold is deg Delta_{n,h-1} minus the degree of the gcd of the maximal minors. | Working proof: the stable law's condition system is R-linear and homogeneous; Cramer and unique factorization at the boundary. | [Pre-stable savings on the cube](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-threshold-ideal) |
| `conj:cube-dimension-three-thresholds` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2: the gcd of the boundary minors is (y1y2y3)^{d^2} prod(y_i-y_j)^{d^2}, so kappa = d+1 at m = 4d is reached exactly from l = d^2 - 1 (the degree of the d-division locus of 2c_1); and delta(3,k,0) = 2k - floor(k/5) for k >= 2. | Both parts are now proved: part 1 by thm:cube-dimension-three-boundary-threshold, part 2 by thm:cube-order-zero-value (lower bound) with thm:cube-order-zero-upper-bound. | [Pre-stable savings on the cube](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-threshold-ideal) |
| `prop:cube-boundary-torsion-coprime` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, every prime factor of the gcd g of the maximal minors of the 4d x (4d+1) boundary constraint matrix is some y_i or y_i - y_j (the matrix has full rank at every point with distinct nonzero entries); hence the savings reach d+1 at m = 4d no earlier than l = degree of the non-collision part of Delta_{3,d}. | Working proof: at every point with distinct nonzero entries the genus-1 curve has L(dH_inf - (4d+1)p0) = 0, so the specialized matrix has full rank; then the threshold-ideal lemma. | [The boundary thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-boundary-gcd) |
| `check:cube-boundary-gcd-degrees` | Along a random line over F_1000003: for n = 3, d <= 10, deg Delta_{3,d} = 7d^2 - 1 and both g and Delta have multiplicity exactly d^2 at each collision root, so l_0 = d^2 - 1; for n = 4, d <= 5, the common exponent is d^2 + (d-1)^2 and l_0 = 0, 15, 55, 115, 195. The per-order kernel at n = 3 over F_101 gives h = 5 at m = 20, l = 23 (k = 44) and h = 6 at l = 24 (k = 45): l_0 = 24 exactly. | Finite check: compiled minors, interpolation and univariate gcds; the line computation certifies the inequality l_0 >= computed value and is evidence for equality. | [The boundary thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-boundary-gcd) |
| `lem:cube-collision-lifts` | Along y_1 = 0 on {0,1}^n (char != 2), the elements P * Psi_{d-e}(y_1 T), for P = T^Q z^r' of weight e in V_{n-1,d-1} and Psi_k the order-k element of the one-variable problem, lift z_1 P with truncation divisible by y_1^{d-e}; so (when the matrix has rank N) v_{y_1}(g_{n,d}) >= E_n(d) = sum_P (d - e(P)), with equality and elementary divisors exactly {d - e(P)} for n = 3. | Working proof: genus-0 one-variable law, explicit lifts, and saturation via injectivity of V_{2,2d} modulo T^{4d+1} (n = 2 law). | [The boundary thresholds in dimension 3 are d^2 - 1](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-collision-exponent) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-boundary-threshold` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2 and every d >= 1, the boundary gcd is c (y1y2y3)^{d^2} prod(y_i-y_j)^{d^2}, and at m = 4d the savings are >= d+1 exactly when l >= d^2 - 1; the threshold generator Delta/g has degree d^2 - 1 and vanishes set-theoretically on the d-division locus of 2c_1. | Working proof: collision lifts along y_i = 0, a Mobius change of parameter for y_i = y_j, the only-collision-factors proposition, deg Delta_{3,d} = 7d^2 - 1, and the threshold-ideal lemma. | [The boundary thresholds in dimension 3 are d^2 - 1](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-collision-exponent) |
| `lem:cube-dual-polynomial-form` | On {0,1}^n over any field, savings >= h at (k,l) iff some polynomial Phi(u) with homogeneous parts in degrees l..l+m (m = k-l-1) and nonzero degree-l part satisfies [Phi * prod_{a_i=1} r_0(u_i)]_{l+m-t} = 0 for all a in {0,1}^n, \|a\| + 2t <= h-1. | Working proof: re-indexing of the threshold-ideal condition system (Phi_{l+m-c} = W_c) and convolution of homogeneous parts. | [Order zero on the 3-cube](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-zero-upper) |
| `thm:cube-order-zero-upper-bound` | Over every field of characteristic != 2 and every k >= 2, delta(3,k,0) <= 2k - floor(k/5): plane products for k = 2, 3, 4 and Vieta-type dual polynomials for k = 5, 6, multiplied. | Working proof: explicit constructions, the dual polynomial form, and multiplicativity; the matching lower bound is only computed (k <= 30 over F_101, k <= 32 over F_3). | [Order zero on the 3-cube](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-zero-upper) |
| `lem:cube-order-zero-local-limits` | For order-zero dual solutions on {0,1}^n (char != 2): an element of order exactly m in any specialization V_d(y*) excludes a solution at m; for n = 3 all such orders are <= 4d, so evaluation excludes only m <= 4d (pointwise solutions exist for m >= 4d+1); and restriction to y_1 = 0 gives a solution for U = V_{n-1,d} + span{T^{d-e(P)} P} (for n = 3, U_d = span{T^Q z^r' : Q + \|r'\| <= d}). | Working proof: specialization of polynomial identities, pole counts on the specialized curves, and the collision lifts. | [Order zero on the 3-cube: why pointwise and single-divisor arguments cannot give the lower bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-zero-obstructions) |
| `check:cube-dual-order-zero-thresholds` | Least m with an order-zero dual solution over F_1000003: 4, 9, 14 for V_{3,d}, d = 1..3 (= 5d - 1), and 4, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29 for the restricted U_d in two variables, d = 1..7 (= 4d + 1 for d >= 2; every m in [4d+1, 5d-2] solvable for d <= 5 per the referee). | Finite check by modular linear algebra on the dual conditions with Phi_0 = 1. | [Order zero on the 3-cube: why pointwise and single-divisor arguments cannot give the lower bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-order-zero-obstructions) |
| `thm:cube-product-threshold-bound` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for 1 <= rho <= d the threshold l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) is at most B(d,rho) = sum (p_i^2 - 1) over the balanced partition of j+q into q = min(rho, j) parts (j = d - rho), and 0 when j = 0: products of boundary witnesses and an order-zero witness. | Working proof: products add multiplicities, origin orders and savings (h1 + h2 - 1), the boundary theorem, the order-zero upper bound, and monotonicity in l. | [Pre-stable thresholds on the 3-cube: products give a torsion-partition bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-torsion-partition-thresholds) |
| `conj:cube-torsion-partition-law` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d,rho) exactly, and the degree-B part of the threshold ideal is spanned by prod Delta_{3,p_i}/g_{3,p_i} (primitive boundary generators); this determines the whole per-order function and gives delta(3,k,0) = 2k - floor(k/5). | Conjecture: every exact computed threshold (d <= 7, including two predicted in advance and 14 at d = 7) equals B, and all partial bounds are consistent; the degree-B parts L_2, L_2^2 at d <= 4 follow from the product structure. | [Pre-stable thresholds on the 3-cube: products give a torsion-partition bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-torsion-partition-thresholds) |
| `lem:cube-gcd-all-m` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for d >= 1 and every m >= 4d the gcd of the maximal minors of the 4d x (m+1) constraint matrix is c (y1y2y3)^{d^2} prod (y_i - y_j)^{d^2}. | Working proof: full rank off the collisions (orders <= 4d), collision lifts saturating at every m >= 4d by the n = 2 law, Mobius transport; fresh-context referee found no gap. | [The 3-cube's constraint minors past the boundary](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-gcd-all-m) |
| `prop:cube-solution-degree-identity` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for m = 4d + rho - 1 >= 4d: if the solution module Sol_m = ker A_m is free, its homogeneous generators' excesses sum to d^2 - 1 - C(rho,2). | Conditional result: Cramer/Plucker duality with the gcd lemma; freeness is unproved. | [The 3-cube's constraint minors past the boundary](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-gcd-all-m) |
| `check:cube-torsion-divisor-saturation` | Over F_1000003 at one random residue point, saturation along y1 = y2 + y3 puts e_m in the reduced saturation at (d,m) = (2,8) but not at (3,13), (4,18) (valuation 0 in all three); along y1 = 0 at (3,13) the valuation is 9 = d^2. | Finite check: s-adic saturation over F_p[[s]] at a random residue point; evidence that the degree-3 lowest part at rho = d-1 is not a divisibility effect. | [The 3-cube's constraint minors past the boundary](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-gcd-all-m) |
| `lem:cube-threshold-zero-scheme` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, with m = 4d + rho - 1: the solution sheaf E_m is locally free of rank rho with c_1 = -(d^2 - 1 - C(rho,2)); for rho >= 2, 0 -> E_{m-1}(1) -> E_m -> J_Z -> 0 with Z zero-dimensional and supported in the seven multiple points of the arrangement y_i = 0, y_i = y_j, so I_m has no common factor and l_0 >= alpha(Z). | Working proof: reflexive sheaves on P^2, the Plucker degree with lem:cube-gcd-all-m, additivity of c_1, full rank off the lines and collision lifts on them, Mobius transport. | [Past the boundary, the 3-cube's threshold ideal lies in the ideal of a finite scheme at the arrangement's multiple points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-cube-threshold-zero-scheme) |

| `conj:family-fall-locality` | Family fall locality (conjecture): for a family of separately augmented complete accuracy-one ENS blocks over F_3 with private coefficients, every block having at least one private input, and cross set R and T as in conj:bounded-linkage-large-h (no W), each subfamily carrying the cross generators of the same rule whose blocks lie in it, the lowest span-ring fall of the family (infinity if none) equals the least lowest fall over its subfamilies of at most three blocks (single blocks have none).
